works.title: Multiparameter Optimization Extends the Lifetime of Cell-Free Protein Synthesis in a High-Throughput Format
works.abstract: Abstract Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) is a powerful platform for synthetic biology, yet the factors governing reaction longevity remain poorly understood despite their importance for high-throughput applications. Here, the three principal determinants of CFPS performanceDNA template design, reaction composition, and lysate genotypewere systematically optimized to extend reaction lifetime in a 384-well plate format. Different energy regeneration systems were evaluated through real-time pH monitoring and metabolomic analyses to identify the metabolic constraints limiting prolonged protein synthesis. Lysates prepared from engineered Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) strains were further examined to assess the contributions of DNA, RNA, and amino acid stabilization. Systematic optimization of amino acid, nucleoside triphosphate, polyethylene glycol, and lysate concentrations identified DNA template stability and amino acid preservation as the primary factors sustaining CFPS activity. Combining these improvements yielded reactions that remained productive for >14 h and produced 567 ± 64 μg mL−1 active deGFP. These findings establish practical strategies for extending CFPS lifetime and improving high-throughput cell-free platforms.

works.title: Versatile Enzyme Immobilization through Genetically Encoded Biomolecular Click Modules on the Spore Surface
works.abstract: Abstract Here, we report engineered bacterial spores for versatile covalent enzyme immobilization through a biomolecular click reaction (Click-TIED). This approach decouples crust protein folding and assembly during sporulation from the production of target enzymes, enabling a versatile immobilization platform. We identified a truncated CgeA protein as an effective fusion partner for successful covalent bond formation on the Bacillus subtilis spore surface. The resulting immobilized enzymes remained stable on the spore surface and showed robust, improved activity for long-term reuse for a week. This platform also enables enzyme co-immobilization for tandem catalysis and the direct harvesting of target enzymes from cell lysates. This work presents a straightforward method for covalently immobilizing enzymes on the bacterial spore, a recyclable and renewable biological bead, advancing the development of a deployable biocatalysis platform.

works.title: Metabolic Engineering of Chromosomally Integrated Bacillus licheniformis for the Efficient Biosynthesis of Pseudouridine
works.abstract: Abstract Pseudouridine (Ψ) is extensively applied in the medical domain, particularly for mRNA vaccines. However, the production titers of the existing engineered strains remain insufficient to meet market demands. In this study, a multilevel metabolic engineering strategy was implemented to achieve high-level Ψ production in Bacillus licheniformis. First, heterologous ΨMP glycosidase was introduced and engineered, resulting in Ψ production of 1.8 g/L. Subsequently, yqfW and yfnB with strong dephosphorylation for ΨMP were overexpressed, elevating Ψ production by 179.3%. Furthermore, carbon flux was redirected toward intracellular ribose-5-phosphate supply via attenuated pgi expression, increasing Ψ production to 12.1 g/L. Finally, scale-up cultivation in a 5 L bioreactor achieved a Ψ titer of 38.6 g/L, with molar conversion rates of 96.5% from uracil and 31.5% from glucose. These results represent the highest Ψ production level reported in Bacillus species to date, providing a robust foundation for the biosynthesis and industrial application of pyrimidine nucleosides.

works.title: Synthetic Biology Strategies for Engineering Microbial Cell Factories toward Efficient p -Coumaric Acid Biosynthesis
works.abstract: Abstract p-Coumaric acid (p-CA) is a high-value phenolic acid with applications in food preservation, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and the production of plant-derived aromatic compounds. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative to plant extraction and chemical synthesis. In this review, recent advances in synthetic biology strategies for microbial p-CA biosynthesis are systematically summarized. The natural biosynthetic pathways and major heterologous routes are first introduced, followed by a review of key enzyme engineering strategies. Furthermore, metabolic engineering approaches for increasing precursor availability, enhancing metabolic flux, attenuating competing branches, blocking degradation pathways, and optimizing cofactor and transporter systems are discussed. Emerging model-guided and machine learning-assisted strategies for rational strain optimization are also highlighted. Finally, progress in chassis reinforcement, substrate expansion, and fermentation process optimization is summarized, and future opportunities for constructing robust, efficient, and industrially applicable p-CA-producing microbial cell factories are discussed.

Modular engineering of aromatic metabolism in Corynebacterium glutamicum enables protocatechuic acid and gallic acid production
works.abstract: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) and gallic acid (GA) are valuable phenolic compounds with diverse pharmacological activities, including antioxidant and antitumor properties, and have broad applications in the food, cosmetic, chemical, and pharmaceutical industries. However, the industrial production of these compounds remains limited by the insufficient performance of current microbial cell factories, resulting in low productivity and high manufacturing costs. Here, an efficient biosynthetic platform based on Corynebacterium glutamicum was systematically established for the production of PCA and GA. Through reconstruction of the PCA biosynthetic pathway, elimination of competing branches in the shikimate pathway, enhancement of the key rate-limiting enzyme, and modulation of the glucose uptake system to increase phosphoenolpyruvate supply, metabolic flux was effectively redirected toward PCA accumulation, resulting in the engineered strain PCA16 achieving a PCA titer of 19.8 g/L in shake-flask fermentation. Building on this platform, GA biosynthesis was established by introducing a mutant pobA from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and further strengthening the shikimate pathway, enabling strain GA06 to produce 7.86 g/L GA in shake-flask fermentation. Upon scale-up in a 5 L bioreactor, GA production was further increased to 25.66 g/L, representing the highest reported titer for GA production using C. glutamicum to date. Overall, this work demonstrates the strong potential of C. glutamicum as a robust microbial chassis for efficient production of PCA and GA, and provides a versatile platform for the biosynthesis of PCA-derived aromatic compounds.

works.title: De novo biosynthesis of meroterpenoid grifolic acid in Yarrowia lipolytica
works.abstract: Grifolic acid, a potent bioactive meroterpenoid derived from fungi, shows great antitumor and antimicrobial properties. Nevertheless, the difficulty of large-scale chemical production and its minimal presence in natural environments hinder its path toward clinical translation. We developed a de novo grifolic acid biosynthetic route by leveraging the robust metabolic capabilities of the oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica . By improving the precursor malonyl-CoA supply through ACC1 overexpression and spatially targeting the fungal polyketide synthase ArmB to the vacuolar compartment, we enhanced orsellinic acid accumulation to 8.50 mg/L. We next leveraged AI-guided molecular docking and deep learning kinetic predictions (CataPro and UniKP) to screen candidate enzymes for coupling orsellinic acid with farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP), identifying StbC from Stachybotrys bisbyi as the optimal prenyltransferase for coupling the polyketide with the terpenoid moieties. Integrating the heterologous module with efflux pump engineering (overexpressing native Pleiotropic Drug Resistance ABC transporters) and blocking the competing β-oxidation pathway (through HBD1 deletion) relieved intracellular toxicity and minimized carbon loss. Under optimized conditions using a two-stage glucose-growth and glycerol-supplementation fed-batch regime, the engineered strain produced grifolic acid at 30.5 mg/L in a shaker flask. This work represents the first successful de novo production of grifolic acid in Y. lipolytica , validating a holistic metabolic engineering strategy for the sustainable synthesis of complex meroterpenoids.

works.title: Beyond Glycan Binding: Defining Professional Glycoconjugate Counterreceptors in Cellular Systems
works.abstract: Glycan-protein interactions can regulate important biological processes yet are often described in simplistic terms of glycan-binding preferences that imply broad and promiscuous recognition. This conventional ligand-receptor paradigm often fails to distinguish simple binding events from functional binding with downstream biological effects observed in cellular contexts. In this review, we formalize the concept of professional glycoconjugate counterreceptors (PGCRs), which are defined as glycoconjugates whose glycan composition and protein scaffold together enable selective engagement by glycan-binding proteins (GBPs) to drive biological function. We review emerging chemical biology, proteomic, and genetic approaches including proximity labeling, crosslinking mass spectrometry, and CRISPR-based screening, that enable context-dependent identification of PGCRs. These studies reveal that glycan recognition is frequently scaffold-dependent and mediated by discrete glycoproteoforms rather than generic glycan motifs alone. Representative examples, such as Gal-3-CD9 and CD43-Siglec-7 interactions, highlight the importance of integrating binding with functional validation. We envision that a framework shift from a glycan-centric to a glycoconjugate-centric view of molecular recognition can improve our understanding of glycan-dependent signaling particularly in the landscape of druggable biology.

works.title: A Critical Single-Point Mutation Enhancing the Catalytic Performance of Flavin-Dependent Halogenase RebH for Chlorination of Aminoquinolines
works.abstract: Abstract Flavin-dependent halogenases (FDHs) are promising biocatalysts capable of installing halogen atoms into aromatic and aliphatic compounds. However, the leakage of hypohalous acid (HOX), primarily caused by the imbalance between HOX generation and consumption rates, impairs their catalytic efficiency and limits practical applications. Herein, a structure-guided engineering strategy was performed to engineer FDH RebH for the efficient chlorination of aminoquinolines. A critical single-point variant, S110P, was screened via a facile high-throughput screening assay. Compared with the wild-type RebH, S110P exhibited 2.0- to 6.0-fold higher specific activity, 38%−94% enhanced catalytic efficiency, and significantly improved thermostability, with a 9.1 °C increase in melting temperature (Tm) and a 3.3-fold extended half-life (t1/2) at 35 °C. Moreover, S110P delivered 1.8- to 13.1-fold higher chlorination yields in 50 mL conversion reactions and showed a broadened substrate scope toward diverse quinolines. Computational analyses revealed that this single-point mutation modulated the conformational dynamics of key functional regions, strengthened HOCl binding in the active site, thereby reducing HOCl leakage by 73.5% over 30 min, and enhanced the propensity to form pre-reaction conformations. This work systematically elucidated the structure−function relationship of FDHs through mutational effect analysis of the critical site and laid an important foundation for their applications in biocatalytic halogenation of electron-deficient quinoline ring.

FlAsH-ID enables live-cell photoproximity labeling with a short peptide tag
works.abstract: Proximity labeling has emerged as a valuable tool for the interrogation of protein–protein and protein–RNA interactions. Almost all proximity labeling methods are deployed using large fusion proteins, which, while powerful in many contexts, can disrupt native biology or obscure important epitopes on the protein under study. Here we develop a photoproximity labeling method that is localized to a short 6-aa peptide sequence. Termed FlAsH-ID, this method uses the combination of the Tsien tetracysteine tag with the FlAsH dye for localized singlet oxygen generation. We demonstrate that this green-light-based method is nontoxic and can be used to label proteins within several cellular compartments. Lastly, we establish that FlAsH-ID can be deployed in primary CD8+ T cells to assess the interactome of the transcription factor RUNX3. Our results suggest this technique will expand the field of proximity labeling to small, functionally sensitive proteins in primary cells without perturbing their function. Commonly used proximity labeling methods implement large fusions of a protein of interest to a proximity labeling enzyme, which can block key protein interactions and disrupt native biology. Now, a method called FlAsH-ID has been developed that enables photoproximity labeling of a protein of interest using a 6-aa peptide tag to bind a small-molecule photocatalyst.

Integrating Synergistic Mutagenesis and Targeted Metabolic Engineering with Process Control for the Hyper-Production of Pyrroloquinoline Quinone in Hyphomicrobium denitrificans
works.abstract: Abstract Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ), a redox-active quinone cofactor with diverse physiological functions, has attracted increasing attention owing to its expanding applications in pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and electrochemical sensing. Microbial fermentation provides a sustainable and scalable approach for PQQ production. In this study, an elite mutant strain, WX17A, was obtained through combined mutagenesis and adaptive laboratory evolution. To further improve PQQ biosynthesis, key fermentation conditions were systematically optimized, and response surface methodology was subsequently employed to optimize the supplementation of exogenous amino acids, metal ions, and hydrogen peroxide. Targeted metabolic engineering further identified PqqC and PqqE as key engineering targets in the PQQ biosynthetic pathway. Rational overexpression of these genes increased the PQQ titer to 134.77 mg/L. Finally, a fed-batch fermentation strategy coupled with two-stage regulation of pH and dissolved oxygen was established in a 5 L bioreactor, resulting in a final PQQ titer of 385.83 mg/L. Overall, the integration of strain improvement, fermentation optimization, metabolic engineering, and process control substantially enhanced PQQ production, providing a promising basis for the development of efficient and scalable PQQ biomanufacturing.

works.title: A conserved urate oxidase helix-tiling assembly promotes metabolic robustness in peroxisomes
works.abstract: Cells organize metabolism within a crowded intracellular milieu, yet the structural logic and functional consequences of supramolecular enzyme assemblies in vivo remain poorly defined. Here, using in situ cryo-electron tomography, we identify a previously uncharacterized high-order architecture of urate oxidase in mouse liver. Urate oxidase homotetramers assemble into helical fibers that tile laterally to form a stable, porous lamellar scaffold. This organization preserves extensive accessible surface area while permitting efficient substrate and product exchange. Structure-guided perturbation abolishes the assembly in vivo without measurably altering intrinsic catalytic activity, indicating a primary role in spatial organization rather than allosteric regulation. Consistent with this, the assembled state enhances resistance to thermal, proteolytic and oxidative stress, supporting sustained activity in the peroxide-rich peroxisomal matrix. Conserved across mammals, this architecture reveals a strategy for metabolic compartmentalization that couples efficient catalysis to increased molecular robustness without the trade-off between supramolecular assembly and enzyme accessibility. Enzyme organization inside cells remains poorly understood. Here, the authors use cryo-electron tomography to show that urate oxidase forms conserved helix-tiling assemblies in liver peroxisomes, stabilizing the enzyme while preserving efficient catalysis.

works.title: Droplet microfluidics-enabled large-scale generation of apical-out human nasal organoids for respiratory virus infection modeling
works.abstract: Human nasal organoids (HNOs) have emerged as promising human-derived models for respiratory virus studies by recapitulating the cellular diversity and infection-related responses of the nasal epithelium. However, scalable generation of HNOs remains technically challenging, limiting their broader application in systematic respiratory virus infection studies and antiviral evaluation. Here, we developed a droplet microfluidics-based platform for the large-scale generation of apical-out HNOs using cell-laden microgels produced from uniform droplets. The platform continuously generated approximately 90,000–120,000 cell-laden droplets per minute, supporting efficient organoid formation with an average efficiency of 71%. The resulting HNOs exhibited apical-out polarity and contained major nasal epithelial cell types. Using human rhinovirus C15 (RV-C15) as a model respiratory virus, we demonstrated that these apical-out HNOs supported productive RV-C15 replication and recapitulated key infection-associated phenotypes, including cell death, innate immune responses, and ciliary damage. Furthermore, these HNOs enabled antiviral drug evaluation, with rupintrivir and itraconazole reducing RV-C15 replication and virus-induced cytotoxicity. We established a droplet microfluidics-based platform for the large-scale generation of apical-out HNOs. By integrating controlled microgel generation, reproducible organoid formation, and direct apical accessibility, this platform provides a scalable and human-relevant approach for respiratory virus infection modeling and antiviral evaluation. Not applicable.

works.title: A genetic engineering toolkit for the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii
works.abstract: Saccharomyces boulardii ( S. boulardii ) is the only yeast probiotic widely used in clinical practice and consumer products. It combines gastrointestinal robustness, intrinsic antibiotic tolerance and eukaryotic protein-processing capacity, making it an attractive chassis for engineered probiotics, in situ biomanufacturing and live biotherapeutic delivery. However, host-specific characterization of regulatory elements, candidate genomic integration sites, and multicopy integration strategies remains limited in the clinically used S. boulardii CNCM I-745 background. Here, using S. boulardii CNCM I-745 as the host, we developed and characterized a genetic engineering toolkit that integrates transcriptional control elements with genome-integration strategies. We first quantified the activities of 20 endogenous constitutive promoters, two inducible promoters and six terminators. We then established a markerless CRISPR-Cas9 workflow and evaluated 10 chromosomal integration loci; six of which showed Editing efficiency above 80% while supporting comparable transgene expression without detectable growth penalties. Finally, we constructed an rDNA-repeat-based multicopy integration system that increased transgene expression by 9.8- to 22.6-fold relative to single-copy integration and revealed a significant positive but non-proportional association between estimated copy number and reporter output. Together, this toolkit provides S. boulardii with a set of tunable promoters and terminators, candidate chromosomal integration sites compatible with a markerless CRISPR-Cas9 workflow. These resources expand the genetic accessibility of this probiotic yeast and provide a foundation for developing engineered S. boulardii strains with enhanced probiotic, therapeutic and biomanufacturing functions.

works.title: Editing the C2 Position of Glycolipid Ligands Reveals Ligand-Dependent Recognition by Mincle
works.abstract: Macrophage-inducible C-type lectin (Mincle) induces immune responses in the presence of pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns, including glycolipids such as trehalose dimycolate (TDM), and is a potential target for the development of vaccine adjuvants. While previous research has extensively explored the structure-activity relationship (SAR) of the lipid component of Mincle ligands, here we focus on structural modification of the C-2 hydroxy group of trehalose in TDM. We previously reported that replacing the 2-hydroxy group of α-glucosylceramide with an exomethylene group significantly enhances its Mincle activation potential. In contrast, we found here that 2-C-substituted pseudo-TDMs, synthesized through a sequential Tsuji-Trost-type reaction, only weakly activate Mincle, suggesting a major role of TDM's C-2 hydroxy group in Mincle activation. Molecular modeling studies provided a rationale for the contrasting effects of C2-exomethylene substitution on trehalose esters and α-glucosylceramide and guided the design of a 2-exomethylene pseudo-α-GlcCer bearing a 6-behenate moiety, which showed enhanced Mincle activation. Our results suggest the existence of multiple binding modes for α-glucosylceramide-type ligands on Mincle.

works.title: Stepwise Optimization and Transcription Factor Engineering for Efficient Ectoine Production in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Abstract Ectoine, a high-value compatible solute, is widely used in cosmetics, biopharmaceuticals, and the pharmaceutical industry. Although non-halophilic chassis such as Escherichia coli are preferred for industrial ectoine production, unclear metabolic distributions and physiological constraints have limited titers and productivity. Here, we report a systematic metabolic engineering strategy for high-performance ectoine biosynthesis in E. coli. Introduction of the ectoine gene cluster from Halomonas elongata, coupled with enhanced flux from phosphoenolpyruvate to l-aspartate-β-semialdehyde, established de novo ectoine production. Combinatorial optimization for promoters and expression of an EctBE407D variant collectively increased the ectoine titer by 353% in strain ECT08. Furthermore, the supply of synthetic precursors l-glutamate and oxaloacetic acid was enhanced, elevating the bioproduct to 9.09 g/L in strain ECT18, coupled with a deliberate downregulation of the TCA cycle flux. Transcriptional regulator screening further identified Lrp as a growth-coupled engineering target, whose manipulation enhanced both titer and biomass by 19.83% and 28.62%, respectively. Importantly, metabolic profiles indicated that the Lrp supervised a multi-node regulatory program that alleviated carbon supply, precursor conversion, nitrogen donor availability, and energy efficiency. In fed-batch fermentation, the final strain ECT31 was cultivated in a 7 L bioreactor and induced at 10 h, producing 81.39 g/L ectoine with a yield of 0.31 g/g and a productivity of 0.75 g/L/h. These systematic strategies establish a robust paradigm for the efficient microbial production of aspartate-derived compounds.

works.title: Structure of chlorophyll synthase in complex with the LHC-like protein HliD
works.abstract: Abstract Chlorophyll synthase (ChlG) is a transmembrane enzyme that attaches the tetraprenyl tail to chlorophyllide to produce chlorophyll a , the key pigment of oxygenic photosynthesis. In the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803, ChlG forms a complex with the light-harvesting complex (LHC)-like high-light-inducible protein (Hlip) HliD. Here, to understand the catalytic mechanism of ChlG and the role of HliD, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to determine the structure of a ChlG 2 HliD 2 complex in substrate-free and geranylgeranyl-pyrophosphate-bound states and AlphaFold to model binding of chlorophyllide at the active site of ChlG. In combination with site-directed mutagenesis and molecular dynamics simulations, our structural data allow us to propose the mechanisms of substrate specificity and catalysis by ChlG. Our structures also reveal how a central HliD homodimer binds two ChlG monomers, as well as the arrangement of the four chlorophyll and two carotenoid pigments bound by the Hlips, and shed light on the evolution of eukaryotic LHC antennae.

Short-chain alcohols fueled orthogonal conversion of pyruvate via a non-natural cofactor
works.abstract: As platform chemicals, short-chain alcohols can serve as energy donors for biocatalytic applications. Ubiquitous nicotinamide cofactors such as nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide mediate energy transfer in biological systems, yet they lack the specificity to channel exogenous reducing equivalents directionally toward targeted products. Herein, we constructed non-natural cofactor nicotinamide cytosine dinucleotide (NCD)-dependent multi-enzyme catalytic cascades that efficiently channeled the reducing power of short-chain alcohols to drive pyruvate conversion. Guided by thermodynamic analysis, NCD-preferring methanol dehydrogenase, formaldehyde dehydrogenase and formate dehydrogenase were coupled with either d -lactate dehydrogenase or malic enzyme. This design overcame the thermodynamic barrier of methanol oxidation and enabled pyruvate reduction and reductive carboxylation. Based on the stoichiometry of complete methanol oxidation, the energy conversion efficiencies reached 81% and 95%, respectively. Furthermore, whole-cell biocatalysis was established for the selective reduction of pyruvate to d -lactate with energy conversion efficiencies of 26% and 41%, respectively, using methanol and formaldehyde as exogenous energy donors. To demonstrate broader application scenarios, other short-chain alcohols were then tested as energy donors. Notably, isopropanol achieved a maximum energy yield of 100% to d -lactate, indicating the orthogonal delivery of exogenous chemical energy into the target product via NCD mediation. Overall, this work develops an efficient non-natural cofactor-mediated biocatalytic strategy that employs short-chain alcohols as efficient fuels for reductive biosynthesis, providing a new and reliable platform for the design and optimization of high-performance biocatalytic redox transformation.

Chemoproteomics Discovery of a Central Nervous System-Penetrant Covalent Inhibitor of PIKfyve
works.abstract: PIKfyve is a lipid kinase involved in regulating protein clearance mechanisms and is a promising target for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. We present the discovery and optimization of a central nervous system (CNS)-penetrant covalent PIKfyve inhibitor, DUN'058, which achieves sustained target occupancy in vivo. Covalent screening hits, identified from chemoproteomics experiments performed in live cells, were rapidly optimized to deliver a brain-penetrant covalent inhibitor of PIKfyve. This covalency centred approach employed a suite of mass spectrometry, biochemical and in vivo assays to optimize compound potency, selectivity, and CNS permeability. The target nucleophile, cysteine 1970, is on a flexible loop that appears distal from the kinase active site, highlighting the power of chemoproteomics screening to identify novel nucleophilic amino acids for covalent modification. DUN'058 achieves efficient covalency at the target cysteine, as well as highly selective covalent and reversible selectivity profiles. Covalent PIKfyve inhibition results in modulation of downstream pathway activity, including activation of the transcription factor TFEB, upregulation of protein clearance pathways, and increased GPNMB transcription and secretion of exosome markers. When dosed in vivo, DUN'058 achieves sustained target occupancy in the brains of mice long after systemic compound clearance. The development of DUN'058 is a demonstration of chemoproteomics-based discovery for a high value CNS target, providing an orally bioavailable and covalent PIKfyve inhibitor.

works.title: Itaconic Acid Production from Corn Stover Hydrolysate by Engineered Escherichia coli with the Weimberg Pathway and Carbon Flux Redirection
works.abstract: Abstract To achieve itaconic acid production using non-food feedstocks, this study constructed an engineered Escherichia coli strain capable of efficiently synthesizing itaconic acid using corn stover hydrolysate as the carbon source. By heterologously expressing cis-aconitate decarboxylase, relieving carbon catabolite repression, eliminating by-product synthesis pathways, deleting isocitrate dehydrogenase, introducing the Weimberg pathway to reconstruct the α-ketoglutarate supply route, and incorporating a feedback-resistant citrate synthase from Corynebacterium glutamicum, the carbon flux was progressively optimized toward the directed synthesis of itaconic acid. Furthermore, this study employed a low-waste alkali pretreatment strategy to obtain corn stover cellulose hydrolysate, thereby reducing waste liquid discharge and minimizing the loss of cellulose and hemicellulose. Using the resulting non-detoxified hydrolysate as the substrate, the engineered strain BI18 achieved an itaconic acid titer of 57.1 g/L in fed-batch fermentation, with a total sugar conversion yield of 0.61 g/g. This production routeintegrating strain engineering, non-food feedstocks, and low-waste pretreatmentprovides a technical reference for itaconic acid biorefining from lignocellulosic biomass.

works.title: Enzyme and Metabolic Engineering Enable High-Level δ-Cadinene Production in Serratia marcescens
works.abstract: Abstract δ-Cadinene is a bicyclic sesquiterpene with fruity and herbal aromas that is widely used in flavors, fragrances, and pharmaceuticals. In this study, Serratia marcescens HBQA7, which carries an integrated MVA pathway and tolerates terpenoid toxicity, was used as the chassis strain. Rational design and site-directed mutagenesis of δ-cadinene synthase from Gossypium arboreum yielded a high-yield variant, G531V. In addition, mutations at key residues S409A, Y411A, D452N, and G531E led to the formation of hedycaryol and germacrene D-4-ol as byproducts. By further constructing fusion proteins and balancing the metabolic flux, we increased the yield to 5.98 g/L after 48 h of shake-flask fermentation. In a 5 L bioreactor, 100 h of fed-batch fermentation yielded a final δ-cadinene titer of 55.7 g/L, the highest level of microbial δ-cadinene synthesis reported to date.

works.title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations
works.abstract: Abstract Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design−Build−Test−Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

works.title: Engineering all human milk oligosaccharide fucosidic linkages in planta
works.abstract: Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are a component of breast milk which improve infant health outcomes by modulating immune responses, inhibiting pathogen adhesion, and promoting healthy gut microbiota. Although their effects are well-documented, few HMOs have been clinically or biochemically studied because only a handful of the simplest HMOs out of >200 species are currently possible to chemically synthesize or produce in microbes via metabolic engineering in microbial hosts. In contrast, plants are naturally adept at biosynthesizing a wide range of complex polysaccharides, and they have recently been established as a heterologous system for HMO production. However, much of the structural diversity of HMOs has not yet been reproduced in a plant, particularly fucosylations. Four fucosidic linkages can be found in fucosylated HMOs, but only Fucα1-2Gal has been biosynthesized in planta. Here, we screened bacterial fucosyltransferases using the model plant Nicotiana benthamiana to produce 3-fucosyllactose (Fucα1-3Glc), lacto-N-fucopentaose II (Fucα1-4GlcNAc), and lacto-N-fucopentaose III (Fucα1-3GlcNAc), demonstrating that all four fucosidic linkages can be made in planta. Just twelve glycosidic linkages make up all the HMOs found in breast milk, and our findings increase the number of linkages made in planta from seven to ten, greatly expanding the variety of HMOs accessible in a plant.

works.title: A biosynthetic paradox implicating dynamic zeaxanthin biosynthesis at the ER-LD interface
works.abstract: Traditional metabolic engineering often treats lipid droplets (LDs) as inert storage sinks and assumes shortening enzyme-substrate distance inherently enhances pathway efficiency. Harnessing Yarrowia lipolytica for zeaxanthin production, we uncovered a pivotal “spatial paradox” challenging this conventional dogma. A selective shielding strategy first identified the hydroxylase Pa CrtZ as the primary biosynthetic bottleneck. Subcellular localization trials revealed that directly targeting Pa CrtZ to the β-carotene-rich LD surface unexpectedly yielded the lowest zeaxanthin relative fraction (9.87%), significantly underperforming compared to cytosolic (27.15%) or peroxisomal targeting (43.16%). To investigate this counterintuitive phenomenon, multidimensional engineering strategies were implemented to boost zeaxanthin accumulation. Subsequently, in situ , label-free stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy unequivocally demonstrated the co-localization of β-carotene and zeaxanthin within LDs, confirming that substrate inaccessibility was not the limiting factor. Guided by principles of LD biogenesis, these findings led us to conceptualize a dynamic endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–LD interface functional microenvironment model. We propose that robust Pa CrtZ-catalyzed hydroxylation is sustained predominantly at transient ER–LD junctions, where hydrophobic β-carotene "skimming" is dynamically synchronized with efficient O 2 and NADPH cofactor exchange. This model redefines lipid organelles as active, organized metabolic hubs beyond mere storage, offering a novel transformative framework for future organelle-targeted metabolic interface design.

works.title: Domain Swapping Reveals Direction-Dependent Compatibility of Fungal Polyketide Synthase–Nonribosomal Peptide Synthetase Off-Loading Domains
works.abstract: Two fungal natural products, hirsutellone and didymellamide, are proposed to be biosynthesized from closely related β-ketoamide intermediates despite producing structurally distinct cyclic products. This unusual biosynthetic relationship raises the question of whether the corresponding polyketide synthase-nonribosomal peptide synthetase (PKS-NRPS) off-loading domains are functionally interchangeable. Here, we identified and characterized HirA, a PKS-NRPS involved in hirsutellone biosynthesis, and used it together with AsolS, a PKS-NRPS involved in didymellamide biosynthesis, as a model system to investigate the compatibility of fungal PKS-NRPS off-loading domains. Heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae established that HirA produces a β-ketoamide intermediate possessing a nonaketide polyketide chain closely related to that generated by AsolS. Reciprocal domain swapping revealed asymmetric compatibility: artificial fusion of the HirA-derived reductase domain to the AsolS assembly line supported productive processing of the AsolS-derived intermediate, whereas reciprocal fusion of the Dieckmann cyclase domain yielded the C18-derived product at a low level but did not produce the expected tetramic acid derivative. These results demonstrate that off-loading activity can be retained following domain swapping between distinct fungal PKS-NRPS systems, but the extent of productive processing is strongly direction-dependent. Taken together, our findings identify direction-dependent compatibility and fusion-site dependence as important constraints for engineering fungal PKS-NRPS off-loading domains.

Double resonant piezoelectric cytometry enables label-free mechanophenotyping of PRPF8-Mutant iRPE cells
works.abstract: Abstract Background Pathogenic PRPF8 variants cause severe retinal degeneration, but their biomechanical correlates in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) remain poorly characterized. We developed and applied a reconfigured double resonant piezoelectric cytometry (DRPC) platform for label-free mechanophenotyping of patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell-derived RPE monolayers (iPSC-RPE, iRPE). Results The DRPC platform enabled real-time estimation of traction-associated surface lateral stress, storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss tangent during monolayer adhesion and maturation. Compared with control iRPE, the patient-derived line carrying the PRPF8 c.5792 C > T variant showed impaired barrier function, downregulation of selected cytoskeletal and contractility-associated genes, a descriptively delayed transition from negative protrusive to positive contractile surface stress, less stable maintenance of positive contractile loading, and different group-mean elastic and dissipative trajectories. These mechanical patterns co-occurred with qualitative differences in F-actin and vinculin organization and reduced integrin α5β1 fluorescence intensity. Conclusions These findings identify exploratory, variant-associated differences in dynamic mechanical response patterns in the studied patient-derived iRPE line ( PRPF8 c.5792 C > T) and support DRPC as a complementary label-free approach for monolayer-scale mechanophenotyping in inherited retinal disease models.

works.title: Computational and experimental analysis for the mismatched DNA recognition mechanism of TaqMutS
works.abstract: DNA holds great potential as a next-generation information storage material due to its high density, stability and low energy consumption. However, high synthesis errors severely limit its practical implementation. Enzymatic error correction based on Thermus aquaticus MutS ( Taq MutS) is efficient and straightforward, whereas its severe non-specific binding to perfectly matched DNA drastically decreases the correction performance. In this work, we systematically analyzed the mechanism of mismatched DNA recognition by Taq MutS through alanine scanning mutagenesis, homologous substitution mutations and molecular dynamics simulations. The results revealed that Taq MutS recognized mismatched sites by sensing the local conformational strain of DNA. Specifically, a cooperative push-pull mechanism mediated by residues S57 and D472 modulated the π-stacking interactions between the key recognition residue F39 and DNA. Meanwhile, the electrostatic synergistic effects of residues K61 and R473 effectively regulated the non-specific DNA binding of Taq MutS. Based on these findings, two mutants (V57S and K61H) were constructed, which exhibited enhanced binding efficiency for mismatched DNA and reduced affinity for perfectly matched DNA. Collectively, this study provided useful error-correction tools for high-efficiency DNA synthesis and laid an important theoretical foundation for the rational design of mismatched DNA recognition proteins.

works.title: Unlocking genetic accessibility in Halomonas bluephagenesis: A high-efficiency transformation chassis enables linear DNA-mediated genome editing
works.abstract: Halomonas bluephagenesis has emerged as a promising chassis for industrial biotechnology distinguished by its halophilic robustness and capacity for open and continuous fermentation. However, its poor transformability has substantially limited rapid, iterative, and automatable strain engineering. Here, we develop a “restriction release” strategy that increases transformation efficiency from approximately 10 2 to 10 7 cfu/μg DNA, rivaling the efficiency of standard laboratory Escherichia coli . A spontaneous IS30 insertion disrupting the type II restriction endonuclease gene notI increased plasmid transformation efficiency by about 2000-fold. Targeted deletion of notI reproduced this phenotype, confirming its role as a major barrier. Further deletion of the DNA phosphorothioation restriction locus dptFGH yielded an additional 10 to 37-fold improvement, generating the highly transformable ΔEPSΔFlgΔNotIΔPTRes chassis. Notably, the enhanced chassis further facilitated two linear-DNA-based editing strategies: direct RecET-mediated pyrF deletion using a linear donor coupled with phenotypic selection, achieving a recombination efficiency of 16.7%, and CRISPR/Cas9-assisted ribDHBA promoter replacement via co-delivery of a gRNA plasmid and a linear donor, achieving an efficiency of 11.1%. Together, these results identify endogenous restriction systems as primary barriers to genetic manipulation in H. bluephagenesis . Stepwise restriction release markedly improves plasmid transformation and enables linear DNA-mediated genome editing, providing an improved genetic platform for the iterative engineering of this industrial halophile. More broadly, this study suggests a practical strategy for overcoming the genetic inaccessibility of other non-model microorganisms and accelerating iterative strain engineering.

works.title: Genome Mining-Driven Discovery of the Sactipeptide Smithiosin in Probiotic, Thermophilic Strain Bacillus smithii
works.abstract: Sactipeptides are a class of ribosomally synthesised and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs), which have a cyclic topology formed by unique thioether crosslinks called sactionines. Sactionines are introduced by radical S-adenosylmethionine (rSAM) enzymes between cysteine residues and the α-carbon of other amino acids. Genome sequencing has revealed many putative sactipeptide biosynthetic gene clusters; however, few sactipeptides have been isolated and characterised. Here, we use genome mining to identify a novel sactipeptide from Bacillus smithii. The novel sactipeptide, named smithiosin, was extracted from the industrially important thermophile B. smithii and characterised as a novel homologue of the previously characterised sactipeptide subtilosin A from B. subtilis. Furthermore, the smithiosin precursor peptide gene was heterologously expressed in the subtilosin A producer Bacillus subtilis 168 without knockout of the native precursor peptide, successfully leading to the production of both subtilosin A and smithiosin. This demonstrates for the first time that a non-native precursor peptide is able to outcompete the subtilosin A precursor for all of the native biosynthetic enzymes in B. subtilis, including the radical SAM enzyme AlbA. It also opens a potential new opportunity for screening non-native precursor peptides with the subtilosin A biosynthetic enzymes via heterologous expression in B. subtilis.

works.title: Digital cell factories for biomanufacturing
Transcription Terminators with Context-Dependent Promoter and Terminator Activities
works.abstract: Abstract A dogma of RNA synthesis is that promoter activity and termination are unrelated processes governed by completely different DNA sequences. Serendipitously, we find that two class II (non-hairpin) terminators for bacteriophage T7 RNA polymerase (RNAP), the natural T7 concatemer junction (CJ) and the artificial vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) terminator, are context-dependent strong promoters for Escherichia coli RNAP. However, the third class II member, the artificial human preproparathyroid hormone (PTH) terminator, is not a promoter. Transcription start site mapping and mutagenesis for CJ and VSV reveal a σ70 extended TGn promoter motif including −11A that is lacking in PTH and the involvement of the −35 box region. Furthermore, results resolve the prior paradox of class II termination apparently occurring only in vitro, not in vivo, enabling demonstration of class II termination in vivo by both T7 and E. coli RNAPs. In addition, engineering of T7 RNAP increases its efficiency of class II termination in vivo. Given that prokaryotic synthetic biology is reliant on class I (hairpin) terminators, with TΦ being almost the only option in constructs for T7 RNAP, recombination is an issue in large constructs. Thus, small class II terminators, now better understood with respect to terminator and promoter activities in the context of various DNA sequences and RNAPs, extend the synthetic biology toolkit.

works.title: Discovery and Characterization of a Highly Active CbCas12a Nuclease and Its Application in Rapid Visual Detection of Porcine Epidemic Diarrhea Virus
works.abstract: Abstract Discovering novel Cas12a homologs with higher activity, relaxed PAM requirements, or broad temperature adaptability is essential for improving CRISPR/Cas12 rapid detection systems, particularly for portable and field-deployable applications. In this study, we conducted bioinformatic mining of metagenomic databases based on the characteristic sequence features of CRISPR arrays to identify Cas12a homologs. Two novel Cas12a homologs, GbCas12a and CbCas12a, were identified. Among them, CbCas12a exhibited pronounced trans-cleavage activity and a broad operational temperature range, making it well-suited for rapid nucleic acid detection. By integrating CbCas12a with reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification, we established a CRISPR/CbCas12a-based detection platform and successfully applied it to the visual detection of Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus. This system demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity, underscoring its potential for diverse rapid diagnostic applications in medicine, agriculture, and other fields.

works.title: Structure-Guided Stepwise Engineering of Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidase Enables HRP- and Cu-Free Cascade Oxidation to a Cefuroxime Side-Chain Precursor
works.abstract: Abstract 2-(Furan-2-yl)-2-oxoacetic acid (2-FOA) is a key precursor for constructing the C7 side chain of cefuroxime. Existing biocatalytic routes depend on a copper-dependent galactose oxidase system requiring horseradish peroxidase (HRP) for activation. To expand biocatalytic alternatives, we characterized FAD-dependent 5-hydroxymethylfurfural oxidase from Methylovorus sp. MP688 (MvHMFO), whose redox cycle eliminates demands for exogenous HRP and metal cofactors. However, MvHMFO showed low activity toward the non-natural substrate 2-furyl hydroxymethyl ketone (2-FHMK). Herein, we adopted a three-stage structure-guided stepwise engineering strategy by sequentially evaluating and combining substitutions from the catalytic core to peripheral loops, achieving cavity expansion and local hydration network reorganization. The optimal variant M4 showed 75.2-fold and 132.3-fold improvements in catalytic efficiency toward 2-FHMK and its aldehyde intermediate, respectively. Applying M4 in an elevated-temperature (40 °C) fed-batch process yielded 6.2 g/L of 2-FOA with a conversion of 88%. This work provides an HRP- and Cu-free HMFO platform for 2-FOA synthesis and an engineering framework for adapting oxidoreductases to non-natural substrates.

works.title: Advancing terpenoid biosynthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Synthetic biology approaches for efficient longifolene production
Editor’s Pick: Wild Bioscience
Integrated metabolic and process engineering of Rhodotorula toruloides for light-driven hydrocarbon production
works.abstract: Long-chain hydrocarbons are bulky chemicals traditionally produced via petroleum refining. Microbial production of these hydrocarbons from renewable resources has attracted much attention, but is limited by precursor accessibility and catalysis efficiency. Here, we combined genetic engineering and photobioprocess optimization for blue-light-driven hydrocarbon production by the oleaginous yeast Rhodotorula toruloides . Cytosolic expression of the Chlorella variabilis fatty acid photodecarboxylase ( Cv FAP) in R . toruloides conferred cells producing 15.0 mg/L hydrocarbons, while targeting Cv FAP to lipid droplets (LDs) via fusion with the LD-associated protein Ldp1 enhanced titer by more than 3-fold. Systematic optimization of blue-light fermentation further doubled hydrocarbon titers. Metabolic rewiring of the pathways related to fatty acid activation, lipid turnover, and carotenoid biosynthesis showed that CRT1 deletion had the most pronounced effect, increasing hydrocarbon titer by 2.5-fold. Additional improvements were achieved by reinforcing free fatty acid supply and increasing CvFAP copy number. The final strain R. toruloides NF72D produced 557.7 mg/L hydrocarbons in flask culture, over 37-fold higher than that by the initial cytosolic expression strain. Collectively, this study demonstrates the importance of proper localization of key enzymes for improved biosynthesis of fatty acid-derived metabolites and a great potential for light-driven production of renewable hydrocarbons by oleaginous yeasts.

works.title: A Small Molecule Inhibitor of the Staphylococcus aureus agr Quorum Sensing System with Low-Nanomolar Potency
works.abstract: The accessory gene regulator (agr) quorum sensing system regulates virulence in certain common Gram-positive bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus. Small molecules that block agr have been reported, but most have modest potencies and warrant further mechanistic characterization. Herein, we report a structure-function study on CP-20, a compound recently shown to inhibit agr in S. aureus by targeting the histidine kinase AgrC. We designed a robust new synthetic route to the CP-20 scaffold, generated a collection of CP-20 analogues, and evaluated their activities in cell-based agr reporter and phenotypic assays. These investigations led to the discovery of a compound, CP-20t, which inhibits agr in S. aureus with low-nanomolar potency and acts on AgrC. CP-20t represents, to our knowledge, the most potent small molecule inhibitor of agr known-bridging the almost 1000-fold potency gap between peptide- and small molecule-based inhibitors-and is a powerful tool to study quorum sensing in S. aureus.

works.title: Glycocalyx Remodeling Shapes Cancer Cell Mechanics
works.abstract: The glycocalyx - a complex meshwork of sugars, proteins, and lipids - coats all human cells and plays a crucial role in cell signaling and immune system regulation. While an understanding of its biochemical functions is emerging, its influence on cell mechanics remains comparably underexplored. Recent evidence suggests that the glycocalyx regulates membrane morphology and cell adhesion, yet its mechanical role has been difficult to study, primarily due to the absence of high-throughput analysis strategies that account for cell-to-cell variability. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating real-time deformability cytometry (RT-DC) with genetic and chemical glycocalyx engineering to tune the glycocalyx state and assess how cell mechanics are affected. Using this approach, we uncovered mechanical adaptations that contribute to promoting cell migration and metastasis. These findings establish glycocalyx remodeling as a regulator of cancer-cell mechanics and a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

works.title: Lysine-Targeted Covalent Inhibition of eIF4E with an Anionic Electrophile Warhead
works.abstract: Covalent strategies offer a powerful route to expand the druggable proteome, yet selective lysine targeting remains difficult due to the high pKa and protonation of the amine side chain. The translation initiation factor eIF4E, an mRNA cap-binding protein that controls nuclear export and translation of oncogenic transcripts, has long been considered an undruggable RNA-binding protein. We apply an anionic electrophile strategy that converts a carboxylic acid within a reversible eIF4E ligand into a vinyl acylsulfonamide warhead, preserving salt-bridge and hydrogen bonding interactions in the cap-binding pocket and facilitating Lys162 deprotonation to enable site-specific engagement. This single-step transformation yields JL-03, a potent covalent eIF4E inhibitor with excellent stability toward biological nucleophiles, consistent with context-dependent activation of the warhead in the binding site. In cells, JL-03 achieves robust target engagement and suppresses translation of the oncogenic driver cyclin D. JL-03 reduces the viability of HOXA9-high acute myeloid leukemia cells with greater potency than reversible eIF4E inhibitors and synergizes with the menin inhibitor revumenib, demonstrating that coordinated transcriptional and translational blockade exhausts leukemic dependencies. These findings establish eIF4E as a tractable covalent target and highlight anionic electrophile installation as a generalizable strategy for lysine-directed covalent inhibitor design.

works.title: Breast milk is an overlooked biofluid for point-of-care biosensing
ORB-TXTL: Cell-Free Expression of Membrane Proteins on Lipid Bilayer-Coated Beads
works.abstract: Abstract Membrane proteins achieve a remarkable range of cellular functions, yet their characterization at high throughputs remains difficult with standard reconstitution methods. Here, we develop on-bead reconstitution into bilayers via cell-free transcription and translation (ORB-TXTL), a platform that uses compositionally tunable lipid bilayer-coated silica beads as scaffolds for cell-free synthesized interacting and integral membrane proteins. ORB-TXTL is fast as it takes only a few hours to integrate membrane proteins onto the beads, which can be extensively washed and seamlessly transferred between reaction buffers to perform assays that are read out by standard laboratory equipment without tagging and sophisticated protocols. We first characterized the lipid interactions of the mechanosensitive channel MscL, then screened 169 Escherichia coli proteins, and identified a systematic dependence of membrane integration efficiency on the number of transmembrane domains. Finally, we functionally reconstituted the E. coli phospholipid synthesis pathway, demonstrating that ORB-TXTL is a tractable and cheap chassis for multienzyme membrane biochemistry.

works.title: A selective TNKS2 inhibitor for tumor-restricted WNT suppression
works.abstract: Hyperactive WNT signaling is a potent cancer driver but clinical translation of WNT inhibitors has been hampered by on-target toxicities. WNT signaling can be constrained through inhibition of the PARP-family enzymes tankyrase 1 (TNKS1) and TNKS2; however, existing TNKS inhibitors suppress WNT signaling in both tumor and healthy tissues. In this Article, we show that genomic loss of TNKS1 on chromosome 8p creates a collateral vulnerability that drives a tumor-restricted dependency on TNKS2 for cellular TNKS activity. Through structure-guided design, we identify a flexible loop in TNKS2 that can be exploited to enable TNKS2-selective drug targeting and we generate a first-in-class TNKS2 inhibitor to drive selective WNT inhibition in TNKS1-deficient cell and organoid models. This work demonstrates a targetable cancer-specific vulnerability in multiple cancer types, providing a new approach for WNT-targeted therapies. Through structure-guided rational drug design, a potent and selective tankyrase 2 inhibitor was developed that enables tumor-restricted suppression of oncogenic WNT signaling in cancer cells that have lost one or both copies of chromosome 8p.

works.title: Biosynthetic tailoring of polyene antifungals
Tackling the Tankyrase twins
BLAST: a blue light-assisted secretion toolkit tunable by reversible protein-protein interactions
works.abstract: Precise control over protein secretion is essential for programming intercellular communication and coordinating complex physiological responses. However, conventional methods relying on transcriptional regulation or chemical induction often lack the spatiotemporal precision and reversibility required to mimic endogenous signaling dynamics. We engineered the Blue Light-Assisted Secretion Toolkit (BLAST), a genetically encoded system that orchestrates protein release from the endoplasmic reticulum via light-tunable protein-protein interactions. BLAST comprises two complementary modules utilizing both light-induced sLID/SspB association (a-BLAST) and LOV2/Zdk1 dissociation (d-BLAST). Both modules harness the highly conserved RXR motif to enforce strict ER confinement in the dark state. Mechanistically, by utilizing non-destructive steric masking rather than enzymatic cleavage, BLAST achieves high temporal resolution with strict reversibility. We demonstrate that both systems can be repeatedly toggled ON and OFF, rapidly arresting cargo release upon light withdrawal to generate highly controlled, pulsatile secretion profiles. Leveraging this dynamic control, we successfully achieved the rapid, robust, and light-triggered secretion of complex therapeutic proteins, including interleukin-12 and insulin. These findings establish BLAST as a generalized, plug-and-play platform for the on-demand delivery of therapeutic proteins. By bypassing transcriptional delays and irreversible activation steps, this non-destructive system significantly expands the optogenetic toolbox for synthetic biology and cell-based therapies.

works.title: Systematic metabolic engineering for trans-aconitic acid production in Aspergillus niger
works.abstract: Trans-aconitate (TAA) is a valuable bio-based chemical for nematicides and polymer synthesis. We repurposed the industrial citrate producer Aspergillus niger for efficient TAA biosynthesis. Heterologous AexA enabled extracellular aconitate export. However, overexpressing aconitases from various sources, targeted to the cytoplasm or mitochondria, failed to increase titers. Although mitochondria proved the optimal site for cis-aconitate accumulation, the bottleneck likely persisted due to thermodynamic constraints. To overcome this, we designed a push–pull strategy: a pull module using mitochondrial MttA to export cis-aconitate to the cytosol, where TbrA isomerizes it to TAA, coupled with a push module enhancing cytosolic acetyl-CoA via the phosphoketolase pathway. Multicopy tbrA expression was critical. The final strain produced 34.30 g/L total aconitate (>90% TAA) in a 5-L bioreactor within 6 days. This work highlights a compartmentalized push–pull strategy exploiting mitochondrial-cytosolic organization to convert a citrate chassis into a high-yield TAA cell factory.

works.title: Functional readouts of neural organoids
Multi-dataset INST 13C metabolic flux analysis reveals robust fluxes but variable metabolite pools
works.abstract: Isotopically non-stationary metabolic flux analysis (INST 13 C-MFA) provides unique insights into cellular physiology but remains limited by low throughput and high experimental costs. This is particularly relevant for emerging C1/C2 bioprocesses, where isotopically stationary 13 C-MFA is generally uninformative due to limited labeling diversity. We developed a miniaturized and automated workflow that combines parallelized transient isotope labeling experiments with high-performance computational analysis to enable INST 13 C-MFA at microliter scale. Applied to an evolved Corynebacterium glutamicum strain growing on ethanol, robotic micro-cultivations with complementary tracers, hot isopropanol quenching, and LC-QToF-MS analytics yielded highly informative datasets. Joint analysis produced the first quantitative flux map of ethanol metabolism in evolved C. glutamicum , revealing strong glyoxylate shunt activity. Multi-dataset INST 13 C-MFA further showed that integrating complementary ILEs increased net flux resolution and preserved flux estimates across tracers and independent experimental runs, while pool size estimates remained dataset-specific. Together, this work establishes a cost-efficient, scalable framework for quantitative fluxomics and its integration into biofoundry pipelines, enabling systematic physiological characterization of microorganisms growing on sustainable C1/C2 feedstocks.

UC Irvine’s BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) Brain Procurement Program for the Center for Multiomic Human Brain Cell Atlas Project
works.abstract: SUMMARY High-quality neurotypical postmortem human brain tissue is essential but difficult to obtain for constructing comprehensive human brain cell atlases. Here we describe the establishment of UC Irvine’s Brain Procurement Program, a coordinated initiative to collect and process neurotypical donor brains for multiomic mapping studies within the NIH BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) consortium. Through partnerships with the Orange County Coroner’s Office, the UC Irvine Willed Body Program, UCI Medical Center, and the Children’s Hospital of Orange County, we have developed standardized workflows encompassing donor identification, postmortem brain recovery and processing, region-of-interest dissection, neurotypical donor selection, and data management. Our experience demonstrates the feasibility of a community-based, multi-institutional procurement framework while highlighting challenges in recruiting neurotypical donors and ensuring demographic representation reflective of Southern California. We further identify opportunities to strengthen outreach and donation pathways. This program provides a scalable model for advancing population-reflective, high-quality human brain cell atlas efforts. Highlights Establish a multi-site pipeline for procuring high-quality neurotypical human brains. Demonstrate feasibility of donor collection across childhood to adulthood. Identify barriers and propose strategies to improve broad donor recruitment.

works.title: Liquid‐Suspendable Metabolic Sensors Allow Real‐Time Oxygen Consumption Monitoring in Caco‐2 and Colon Organoid‐Based Gut‐on‐a‐Chip Models
works.abstract: The organ-on-a-chip field is a rapidly evolving area of expertise, combining enhanced physiological relevance with a wide range of functional readouts across diverse cellular models. One such readout is oxygen metabolism, which serves as a key indicator of mitochondrial function. In this study, we utilized metabolic sensors designed for real-time measurement of oxygen consumption, reflecting aerobic respiration, within a commercially available microfluidic platform. We demonstrated that time-resolved detection of oxygen consumption is feasible within the system's microliter-scale volumes and that chemically induced changes in cellular oxygen metabolism can be monitored in real time in two ready-to-use gut-on-a-chip models. In summary, this novel application of metabolic sensors enables direct evaluation of mitochondrial function in complex cellular environments by addressing key analytical challenges often encountered in organ-on-a-chip systems due to their limited size and structural complexity.

Wenting, et al., “Application and Progress of Highcontent Imaging in Molecular Biology,” Biotechnology Journal 18, no. 12 (2023): e2300170, https://doi.org/10.1002/biot.202300170. works.title: Redirecting Metabolic Flux to Minimize By‐Product Formation Enables Efficient De Novo Biosynthesis of Chlorogenic Acid in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Chlorogenic acid (CGA) is an important natural hydroxycinnamic acid ester with diverse biological activities, including antioxidant, antibacterial, and potential antitumor properties. However, efficient microbial titer of CGA remains challenging because of insufficient hydroxylation efficiency, by-product accumulation, and limited host tolerance. Herein, an efficient and sustainable microbial platform for de novo CGA biosynthesis was constructed in Escherichia coli. Enhancement of the NAD(H) biosynthetic pathway increased intracellular reducing power and increased hydroxylation efficiency. A synergistic hydroxylation module consisting of the p-coumarate 3-hydroxylase from Saccharothrix espanaensis (SeC3H) and the flavin reductase from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PaHpaC)was further introduced to promote the conversion of p-coumaric acid (pCA) to caffeic acid (CA) and redirect metabolic flux toward CGA biosynthesis. Rational engineering of 4-coumarate-CoA ligase from Arabidopsis thaliana (At4CL) increased substrate selectivity and decreased the formation of the major by-product p-coumaroylquinic acid (pCQA). In addition, transcriptomic analysis identified lsrG, a gene associated with the AI-2 quorum-sensing system, as a beneficial target whose overexpression further enhanced CGA titer. The final engineered strain produced 7220.3 mg/L CGA in a 50 L fed-batch fermentation. The strategies developed herein may provide an effective metabolic engineering framework for the sustainable biosynthesis of CGA and other aromatic natural products.

works.title: Toward industrial microalgae-based monoclonal antibody production
works.abstract: Over the past two decades, Chinese hamster ovary cells have dominated monoclonal antibody (mAb) production. Although this mammalian cell system carries high operational and capital costs, it aligns well with regulatory requirements for producing high-value, modest-scale therapeutics. However, microalgal systems offer the benefits of light-driven growth, low-cost media, and the potential for significant and efficient scalability, providing a promising route for producing lower-cost mAbs. Reducted production costs and increased scale open novel market opportunities well beyond the therapeutic space. Here, we investigate the history of mAb production in microalgae, the recent molecular and bioprocessing advances that are likely to contribute to their industrial production, and the novel applications that could arise given access to lower-cost mAbs.
