works.title: Comparison of Wildtype and Recombinant Adeno‐Associated Virus (AAV) Production Reveals Distinct Productivity and Content Ratio Profiles
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Recombinant adeno‐associated virus is a leading viral vector for gene therapy. However, recombinant adeno‐associated virus production systems have low titer and content ratio (ratio of genome‐containing to total adeno‐associated virus capsids), making it difficult to generate the large number of vector genomes required for clinical or commercial use. In contrast, wildtype adeno‐associated virus achieves over ten‐fold higher titer compared to recombinant adeno‐associated virus and a content ratio of over 95% full. Despite the higher productivity of wildtype adeno‐associated virus, the mechanisms behind its productivity remain poorly understood. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel wildtype adeno‐associated virus production platform in suspension human embryonic kidney cells across varying multiplicities of infection of adeno‐associated virus to adenovirus. The impact of cellular viral genome delivery mechanisms and the interplay between adeno‐associated virus and its adenoviral helper were investigated by comparing infection‐based systems with transfection‐based and infection–transfection hybrid systems. Wildtype and hybrid infection systems had remarkably different host cell growth profiles and viral gene expression patterns, and achieved over a log‐fold higher titers and 45% higher content ratios, reaching 8.1 × 10 12 vector genomes/mL culture and 72.2% full, compared to recombinant transfection systems (1.63 × 10 11 vector genomes/mL and 26.9% full).

works.title: Mapping the Sequence Preference of the Generalist Class II Lanthipeptide Synthetase ProcM by mRNA Display
works.abstract: The biosynthetic machineries of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) are often substrate tolerant. A remarkable example is the class II lanthipeptide synthetase ProcM, which naturally functions as a generalist enzyme that has not evolved to use a specific substrate during its evolutionary history. Although ProcM has been studied extensively, the sequence features associated with productive modification remain underexplored. In this study, we use the ultrahigh-throughput mRNA display technique to map the sequence compatibility of ProcM across a focused library. This approach expands the landscape of ProcM reactivity beyond native substrates and individually characterized variants. Machine learning (ML) analysis revealed that the dataset contains sequence patterns associated with ProcM reactivity, with models achieving a balanced accuracy of 0.73. This moderate predictive performance contrasts with the near-perfect accuracy reported for specialized enzymes. This finding suggests that predicting substrate compatibility for generalist enzymes is more challenging due to uneven representation of reactive and nonreactive sequences and limitations of the available data. Our results provide a high-throughput view of ProcM reactivity and highlight differences with previous high-throughput studies on substrate selectivity of RiPP modification enzymes. Future studies will need to assess whether these differences are common when comparing generalist with specialist enzymes.

works.title: Nuclear Functional Divergence and Genetic Basis of Cap Colour Variation Revealed by T2T Genomes of Two Compatible Monokaryons in Pholiota adiposa
works.abstract: Basidiomycete fungi maintain a dikaryotic state throughout their life cycle, in which two genetically distinct haploid nuclei coexist within the same cytoplasm. However, the extent and functional significance of inter-nuclear genomic divergence remain poorly understood. Here, we present the first telomere-to-telomere assemblies of two compatible monokaryons (D1 and D11) from a wild isolate of Pholiota adiposa, achieving 13 complete chromosomes with zero gaps and Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs completeness of 98.6% and 98.3%, substantially outperforming the previous fragmented assembly. The two nuclei exhibit only 75% collinear genes, with 570 (D1) and 668 (D11) strain-specific genes. D1-specific genes are enriched in energy metabolism, consistent with faster mycelial growth, while D11-specific genes are enriched in genetic information processing and mitogen-activated protein kinase signalling, revealing functional complementarity between the two haploid nuclei. Resequencing of 18 wild accessions identified two candidate regions associated with red pileus colour on chromosomes 6 and 12, the former as a major-effect locus and the latter harbouring multiple pigment-associated genes. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment implicated phenylalanine metabolism, tyrosine metabolism, and terpenoid biosynthesis in colour formation, suggesting coordinated regulation across metabolic networks. This framework facilitates dissection of nuclear functional divergence and provides candidate targets for understanding fungal phenotypic variation.

works.title: Programmable Synthetic Condensates to Enhance Circuit Robustness for Improved Bioproduction in Bacillus subtilis
works.abstract: Abstract Genetic circuit reliability is often limited by growth-mediated dilution. However, developing an efficient strategy for maintaining reliable circuit function against dilution effects remains a challenge. Here, we introduce programmable condensates to stabilize circuits in Bacillus subtilis. First, we engineered synthetic condensates and employed RIAD/RIDD peptide pairs to selectively sequester the transcription factor (TF). Spatial recruitment of these TF-filled condensates to target promoters facilitated a significant enhancement in gene expression. By tailoring the physicochemical properties and spatial distribution of the condensates, we substantially reinforced the buffering capacity of the circuits at higher temperatures. As a proof of concept, we harnessed this strategy to significantly improve the bioproduction of alkaline protease and 2′-fucosyllactose, achieving a 109.3% increase in enzyme activity and a 108.9% increase in product titer, respectively. Overall, this work offers a valuable toolkit for B. subtilis applications and a programmable framework for robust circuit redesign in other hosts.

works.title: Opportunities and Challenges of Overflow Metabolism in Industrial Microorganisms
works.abstract: Abstract Overflow metabolism represents a ubiquitous phenomenon in industrial microorganisms, characterized by the excretion of organic acids and other byproducts under aerobic, nutrient-rich conditions. While this trait enables rapid cell proliferation, it compromises the carbon utilization efficiency, impairs cellular performance, and limits industrial applicability. Traditional industrial strategies mainly focused on optimizing fermentation conditions to alleviate overflow metabolism. Recent advances have deepened our understanding of the core mechanisms underlying overflow metabolism, including carbon flux imbalance, membrane spatial crowding, protein resource allocation, and redox perturbation. This review systematically summarizes recent research progress on the underlying mechanisms of overflow metabolism as well as the targeted modification strategies developed to modulate this metabolic trait. An in-depth, multifaceted investigation of the drivers of overflow metabolism will facilitate the development of a robust microbial chassis with reduced overflow metabolism and improved bioproduction efficiency.

works.title: DMSG-VBM: Deep Multi-Source Graph-Enhanced Variational Bayesian Model for Predicting Higher-Order Microbe-Drug-Disease Associations
works.abstract: Abstract Exploring potential relationships among drugs, microbes, and diseases is critical for advancing disease prevention and drug development. Several computational models have been developed to predict high-order interactions in multi-omics biological systems. However, negative sampling-based methods risk generating false negatives, whereas tensor decomposition approaches typically require extensive hyperparameter tuning and exhibit limited flexibility when handling complex data architectures. To address these limitations, we propose DMSG-VBM, a Bayesian Logistic Tensor Decomposition model incorporating multi-source graph deep learning. The model employs multi-source graph deep learning to generate prior expectations of latent variables while establishing an attention mechanism to facilitate the integration of multi-source features. Furthermore, DMSG-VBM integrates tensor-based Bayesian inference with multi-source graph deep learning within a probabilistic graphical model and adopts a variational expectation-maximization algorithm for adaptive inference of model parameters and latent variables. Experimental results across four scenarios on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that DMSG-VBM achieves superior performance in triplet prediction compared to other state-of-the-art methods, for both balanced and extremely imbalanced scenarios. Additionally, it exhibits higher hit rates in predictive tasks involving novel drugs, novel microbes, and novel diseases. Case studies further substantiate that DMSG-VBM effectively predicts potential associations among drugs, microbes, and diseases. The codes and dataset are available at: https://github.com/Mayingjun20179/DMSG-VBM.

works.title: In vivo-compatible spatial multi-omics via hydrogen peroxide-independent APEX2 labeling
ESMRank: learning-to-rank prediction of missense variant effects from deep mutational scanning data
works.abstract: Abstract Predicting the functional effects of missense variants is limited both by predictor performance and by the lack of principled strategies to integrate heterogeneous multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs), including deep mutational scanning, into transferable sequence-function models. Here, we show that redundancy among partially overlapping deep mutational scanning experiments, often treated as noise, yields a consensus landscape of mutational constraint. We introduce “variant soundness”, an overlap-aware rank-fusion score that uses cross-experiment consistency to derive an assay-agnostic ordering of mutational tolerance within proteins. Applied to ~1100 MAVEs spanning over two million missense variants, this approach reveals a mutational landscape enriched for structural stability constraints. Guided by this integrated signal, we develop ESMRank, a sequence-based learning-to-rank predictor combining ESM2 representations with physicochemical descriptors. Under strict protein-level partitioning, ESMRank outperforms widely used predictors across abundance-, folding-, and stability-related assays in ProteinGym and Domainome. Predicted deleterious variants are enriched for ClinVar pathogenicity and, in CFTR, correlate with folding efficiency, channel activity, and pharmacological responsiveness. Together, these results turn assay redundancy into a scalable resource for interpretable missense variant prediction.

A mosaic T7 phage platform enables simultaneous display of two independent peptides on the same phage particle. The modular design integrates receptor targeting, protein capture, and tissue-directed in vivo phage display, establishing a versatile methodology for multifunctional phage engineering, receptor identification, and next-generation combinatorial library design.

works.title: A BromoTag-Based Toolkit for Rapid Modulation of Chemically Induced Proximity
works.abstract: Mammalian cells control a wide range of essential processes via protein-protein interactions (PPIs), including signal transduction, gene expression, cell cycle regulation, and metabolism. Pathologic alterations in PPIs have been linked to many human diseases. Thus, the ability to rapidly and selectively induce PPIs in cultured cells is crucial for many fields of biological research. One proven approach is the use of synthetic bivalent chemical ligands to selectively recruit protein domains with engineered mutations (i.e., "bump-and-hole"). Developing new PPI chemical inducers with unique protein domains enables multiplexing and potentially expands the breadth of recruitable proteins. Herein, we describe the design and characterization of a BromoTag- and dTAG-based toolkit to induce protein homo- and heterodimerization. Using a NanoBiT split-luciferase assay, we characterized a library of BromoTag-based homo- (BromoTag/BromoTag) and heterobivalent (BromoTag/dTAG) compounds for their ability to induce neo-PPIs. Compounds were evaluated for activity across multiple cellular applications, including caspase-9 and c-Kit tyrosine kinase activation, with comparable activity to other dimerizer systems. This BromoTag-based protein dimerization toolkit provides a useful alternative to current controlled dimerization systems that will enable robust prototyping of chemically induced proximity.

works.title: A 1,2-Dioxetane-Based Chemiluminescent Probe for In Vivo Copper Imaging
works.abstract: Copper is involved in healthy physiology and aberrant pathology with prominent roles in Wilson's and Menkes diseases. Tracking its reactivity in living systems is crucial to understanding its biological function and could be helpful in identifying targeted therapies. We developed a turn-on chemiluminescent copper probe CpCL, which was designed by linking a picolinic acid moiety to the phenolic substituent of a spiroadamantane 1,2-dioxetane. Reaction of CpCL with copper results in formation of a copper complex intermediate that releases the phenolate upon hydrolysis, followed by initiation of a chemiluminescence reaction for light emission. The probe displayed excellent selectivity for Cu2+ compared to other competitive metal ions, with a sensitive limit of detection of 360 nM. The mechanism was studied using initial rate kinetics to provide an estimated pseudo-first-order rate constant of 5.18 ± 0.38 × 10-5 s-1 for the hydrolysis of the copper-bound probe. The probe was then validated in living mice using the copper chelator ATN-224 as a negative control, demonstrating that it can be used to monitor copper ions in vivo.

works.title: Flavin Cofactor Engineering Rewires Metabolism and Modulates Stress Response in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Abstract Cofactors such as flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, coenzyme A, and S-adenosylmethionine are essential for primary metabolism. Interestingly, they share a common adenosine moiety that does not contribute directly to catalysis and is therefore amenable to engineering for synthetic biology applications. In FAD biosynthesis, the adenosine group is installed by the flavin mononucleotide adenylyltransferase (FMNAT) domain of the bifunctional FAD synthetase using FMN and ATP. This study explores the nucleotide selectivity of the Escherichia coli FMNAT domain and the physiological effects of FAD nucleotide analogues synthesized from cellular nucleotides other than ATP. First, we engineer the FAD synthetase enzyme at an active site loop to produce FAD nucleotide analogues. Chromosomal substitution of the wild-type E. coli FAD synthetase with the mutated version results in the intracellular synthesis of these noncanonical FAD nucleotide analogues and confers tolerance to aminoglycoside antibiotics. Upon investigating their potential downstream metabolic roles, we find that the intracellular production of FAD nucleotide analogues perturbs cellular metabolism and the FAD analogues may bind to a range of E. coli enzymes. These findings validate the FMNAT domain loop as a viable site for cofactor engineering, with potential for synthetic biology. Finally, the observed correlation between FAD analogue production and increased tolerance to aminoglycosides suggests the existence of unexplored metabolic mechanisms underlying antibiotic sensitivity.

works.title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives
works.abstract: Abstract Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design−build−test−learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

works.title: Expanding the catabolic capacity of Pseudomonas putida to acetovanillone, 5-carboxyvanillate, and vanillyl glyoxylate for muconate production from kraft lignin-derived aromatics
works.abstract: The pulp and paper industry produces large volumes of condensed kraft lignin, which is challenging to convert to single chemical products. For this purpose, tandem chemical depolymerization and bioconversion to a single atom-efficient product is a potentially promising strategy. In this study, we conducted copper-catalyzed oxidative depolymerization using pine-derived kraft lignin to generate multiple bioavailable aromatic monomers at a yield of 4.5 weight% (wt%; g monomers per g lignin) from both C–O and C–C bond cleavage, followed by counter-current extraction with a 52 wt% monomer recovery. This resulted in an oxidized lignin product containing vanillin, vanillate, 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde, 4-hydroxybenzoate, 5-formylvanillin, 5-carboxyvanillin, 5-carboxyvanillate, acetovanillone, and vanillyl glyoxylate. Based on this stream composition, we engineered the industrially relevant soil bacterium Pseudomonas putida KT2440 to catabolize the latter five compounds via overexpression of ten heterologous genes ( acvABCDEF SYK-6 , vceAB SYK-6 , ligW2 SYK-6 , and mdlC PP ). We combined these engineered pathways with previously reported strategies for muconate production from G- and H-type monomers to generate P. putida KMM428, which utilized 93.6 ± 0.2 mol% of the quantified aromatic monomers in a depolymerized kraft lignin mixture, and produced muconate at a yield of 99 ± 3 mol%, on a quantified monomer basis. Together, this work increases the theoretical carbon conversion efficiency of this process by 37.6 ± 0.1 mol% through incorporation of three β-5 cleavage products, in addition to traditional G-type monomers.

works.title: An integrated strategy to reprogram NRPS initiation modules for long-chain surfactin biosynthesis
ADP-ribose induces neuronal ferroptosis through ENT2-mediated nucleotide rewiring
An mRNA–lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection
works.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

works.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo
Pathology-informed hydrogel design for myocardial infarction repair: engineering criteria, standardized evaluation, and clinical translation
works.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) produces coupled structural and biological injury that evolves across overlapping and spatially heterogeneous pathological contexts. Existing reviews have commonly summarized hydrogel material classes, therapeutic cargos, delivery routes, or individual mechanisms, but less attention has been given to translating post-MI pathology into measurable engineering criteria, explicit evidence boundaries, and structured translational requirements. This conceptual narrative review addresses this gap using a pathology-informed engineering framework supported by targeted literature searches in PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection. The review links pathological and delivery-related challenges to hydrogel design requirements, measurable material properties, therapeutic strategies, and validation endpoints. It organizes the hydrogel design space using orthogonal descriptors of material origin, network behavior, functional attributes, and architecture; compares injectable, patch-based, cellular, extracellular-vesicle, protein, drug, and nucleic-acid delivery strategies; and defines engineering criteria for mechanics, viscoelasticity, injectability, adhesion, degradation, release, electrical function, responsiveness, and biological validation. Mechanistic plausibility, small-animal efficacy, large-animal evidence, first-in-human safety/feasibility, and demonstrated clinical benefit are treated as distinct evidence levels. Advanced multifunctional systems are evaluated through benefit–trade-off–validation relationships, while clinical translation is considered through manufacturing, CMC, device compatibility, safety, clinically meaningful endpoints, and sequential product-development gates. Future cardiac hydrogel development should be context-aware rather than assigned to fixed post-MI stages, quantitatively characterized using method-appropriate measurements, and advanced according to evidence appropriate to the intended use and development phase. Emphasis on minimum sufficient functionality, reproducible evaluation, clinically realistic delivery, manufacturing feasibility, and safety may improve comparison across platforms and help prioritize candidates for further translational development.

works.title: Improved Biosynthesis of Ethylene Glycol From Xylose in Engineered E. coli Utilizing Two‐Stage Dynamic Control
works.abstract: ABSTRACT We engineered Escherichia coli for improved ethylene glycol (EG) biosynthesis using two‐stage dynamic metabolic control coupled with pathway optimization. An engineered Dahms pathway ( xylB, xylC, xylD, yqhD ) was induced upon phosphate depletion to enable EG biosynthesis during stationary phase. The performance of our initial strain, expressing a baseline pathway, was improved by the addition of “stoichiometric” valves enabling proteolytic degradation of xylose isomerase and soluble transhydrogenase, upon phosphate depletion. Reduction of these enzymes, which compete for substrates with EG biosynthesis, led to a 3‐fold increase in specific productivity. In contrast, enabling “regulatory” dynamic metabolic valves targeting enoyl‐ACP reductase and glucose‐6‐phosphate dehydrogenase, designed to enhance NADPH flux, did not improve production in this control. Following pathway optimization, regulatory strains exhibited enhanced production rates exceeding 0.5 g gCDW − 1 h − 1 , a 14‐fold improvement over the control, while stoichiometric valves conferred no benefit. Scale‐up in fed‐batch bioreactors achieved 140 g L − 1 EG in 70 h with a yield of 0.38 g g − 1 xylose (92% of theoretical), representing one of the highest reported titers in E. coli . These results demonstrate that optimal engineering strategies shift with pathway capacity. While elimination of competing fluxes benefits low‐flux systems, high‐flux pathways require enhanced cofactor regeneration.

works.title: Engineering Mosaic T7 Bacteriophages for Dual Peptide Display to Enable Cellular Targeting and Ligand‐Directed Protein Capture
works.abstract: Integrating molecular recognition, tracing, and interactome capture within a single nanoparticle could allow for probing, manipulation, and control of complex biological systems. Achieving such multifunctionality within a single well-defined nanostructure remains challenging. T7 bacteriophage-based biological nanoparticles provide a robust and genetically programmable scaffold; however, conventional T7 display systems typically accommodate only one exogenous peptide species per phage particle, limiting multifunctional and combinatorial applications. Here, we describe a mosaic phage platform that enables the simultaneous display of two peptides on separate T7 coat protein subunits. By combining genome-encoded and plasmid-driven expression of peptide-fused capsid proteins, the system provides a modular route for assembling multifunctional phage nanoparticles. We generated mosaic T7 phages co-presenting the neuropilin-1 (NRP-1)-binding peptide RPARPAR alongside either a HA-tag or a Twin-Strep (Tstrep) tag affinity handle. These engineered phages specifically target NRP-1-expressing cells and enable immunofluorescence visualization and pull-down of NRP-1 from complex lysates. Furthermore, a random peptide T7 phage library co-displaying the constant lung-homing peptide RPARPAR shows preferential pulmonary accumulation in vivo, demonstrating utility for combinatorial targeting and tissue-directed phage selection. Collectively, this dual-display approach expands phage display by enabling cell targeting, visualization, molecular interactome probing, and in vivo tissue homing within a single genetically encoded nanoparticle platform.

works.title: Issue Information: Biotechnology Journal 11/2026
ARTP Mutagenesis and Omics‐Guided Target Validation for Improved Human Serum Albumin Fusion Protein Production in Yeast
works.abstract: Efficient production of human serum albumin (HSA) fusion proteins in yeast remains constrained by the combined demands of folding, secretion, and cellular resource allocation. Rational optimization of endoplasmic reticulum folding and unfolded protein response pathways can improve production, but additional cellular constraints may persist in engineered strains. Here, we combined iterative atmospheric and room-temperature plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis, activity-coupled screening, and genome- and transcriptome-guided validation to improve production of an amylase-HSA fusion protein (AGSH) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Using extracellular α-amylase activity as the screening indicator, five rounds of ARTP mutagenesis in the folding-optimized strain AH28 generated mutants with enhanced AGSH production. The final mutant N5S14 reached 2.12-fold the AH28 level in AGSH-associated α-amylase activity. Physiological profiling showed that enhanced production was associated with altered growth-production balance and changes in glucose, ethanol, and glycerol profiles. Whole-genome sequencing identified 33 candidate mutation sites, and reverse engineering validated genes associated with improved AGSH production, including BUD27, NPR3, NPR2, and IML1. RNA-seq revealed distinct transcriptional states involving central carbon metabolism, protein folding, and stress-related processes. Transcriptome-guided validation identified PFY1 deletion and SSA3 overexpression as additional beneficial interventions. Overall, this strategy improved AGSH production and identified engineering targets beyond previously optimized folding-related modules.

works.title: Small-Molecule Inhibitors of Cholesterol Sulfotransferase as Immunomodulatory Agents
works.abstract: Though immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy has been a promising advance in cancer treatment, response rates to ICB are low owing to other mechanisms that cancers employ to evade the immune system. SULT2B1b is an enzyme known to produce cholesterol sulfate (CS), an immunosuppressive metabolite that inhibits T-cell migration. Cancers expressing high levels of SULT2B1b thus generate a tumor microenvironment that excludes T cells, which leads to increased tumor growth and renders ICB therapy ineffective. Here, we identify a novel class of azasteroid SULT2B1b inhibitors with greater potency and selectivity than previously identified compounds. X-ray co-crystal structures indicate that these inhibitors bind in a conformation different from that of native substrates, enabling inhibition without acting as a substrate. Additionally, these new compounds effectively reduce CS levels in tumors in mice and, as such, have potential as cancer therapeutics in combination with ICB therapy.

works.title: Directed Evolution of the Cbx1 Chromodomain Generates a High-Affinity Trimethyllysine-Binding Variant
works.abstract: Directed evolution is a powerful and versatile strategy for engineering proteins with enhanced affinity and tailored molecular recognition properties. Here, we applied phage display-guided directed evolution to enhance the binding of the wild-type Cbx1 chromodomain (Cbx1-CD) to an H3K9me3-containing peptide. Screening a soft-randomized library targeting residues surrounding the aromatic cage yielded C29, which bound the H3K9me3 peptide with a KD of 57 nM and exhibited an approximately 14-fold lower dissociation rate constant than Cbx1-CD. Across an H3K9me3-derived alanine-scanning series and a peptide panel, C29 showed stronger binding signals than Cbx1-CD for multiple peptides containing trimethyllysine (Kme3), suggesting lower flanking-sequence dependence for C29 than for Cbx1-CD. An AlphaFold3 model of the C29-H3K9me3 complex suggested local changes in the hydrophobic and electrostatic environment surrounding the Kme3-binding pocket, providing a mechanistic hypothesis for C29's enhanced affinity and reduced flanking-sequence dependence. When two Kme3-containing peptides were spiked into a 100-fold molar excess of unmodified background peptides, C29-conjugated beads effectively enriched both Kme3 peptides relative to the unmodified background. These findings define C29 as a high-affinity Kme3-binding Cbx1 chromodomain variant and support its further evaluation as an affinity reagent for Kme3-containing peptide enrichment.

works.title: Oxidized 5-Methylcytosines and Nucleosome Architecture Cooperatively Influence Thymine DNA Glycosylase Activity
works.abstract: Active DNA demethylation is a fundamental epigenetic process in which the iterative oxidation of 5-methylcytosine (5mC) by TET dioxygenases generates diverse combinations of oxidized 5-methylcytosines within CpG dinucleotides before their excision by thymine DNA glycosylase (TDG). Although heterogeneous CpG oxidation states are expected to arise frequently during this process, how the modification state of the opposing cytosine influences TDG activity remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a chemically defined panel of CpG substrates containing cytosine, 5mC, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), 5-formylcytosine (5fC), and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC) opposite a target 5fC and systematically examined TDG-mediated excision in both naked DNA and nucleosome core particles (NCPs). In naked DNA, opposing-strand cytosine modifications exerted only modest effects on TDG activity when a single excisable base was present within the CpG dyad, whereas dual-substrate CpGs exhibited unexpected differences in strand utilization. In contrast, nucleosome assembly profoundly altered TDG activity, revealing modification-dependent effects that were largely absent in naked DNA and dramatically redistributing strand utilization within dual-substrate CpGs. Together, these findings demonstrate that the oxidation-state composition of a CpG dyad and nucleosome architecture cooperatively regulate TDG activity, establishing heterogeneous CpG oxidation states as functionally distinct substrates for TDG and providing a biochemical framework for understanding how chromatin structure regulates active DNA demethylation.

YlYxc1, an ER-associated alkaline ceramidase of Yarrowia lipolytica, has the hydrolytic activity of ceramides, which can be exploited as a metabolic engineering target to enhance long-chain base production.

works.title: Gut Delivery of Pentameric GLP-1 Using Genetically Engineered Bacillus subtilis
works.abstract: Abstract Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and GLP-1 analogs are widely used for type 2 diabetes (T2D) and weight management, but current approaches can be limited by manufacturing complexity, cost, formulation requirements, and the need for repeated administration. Living microbial delivery systems offer a potential strategy for sustained gastrointestinal production of therapeutic peptides, but achieving stable expression, intestinal survival, and biologically relevant systemic exposure remains challenging. Here, we developed an engineered Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis) spore-based platform for the gastrointestinal delivery of pentameric GLP-1. By leveraging the stress resistance, storage stability, and genetic tractability of B. subtilis, we generated a chromosomally integrated strain that secretes a multimeric GLP-1 construct designed to be processed in the intestine into monomeric GLP-1 peptides. Oral administration of engineered spores resulted in a mean serum GLP-1-related peptide concentration of 20.61 and 23.96 nM on days 3 and 5, respectively, in the first trial and 18.72 and 29.27 nM on days 3 and 7, respectively, in an independent second trial, with minimal detectable signal in green fluorescent protein (GFP) spore-treated controls. Treatment was also associated with preliminary glucose-lowering activity in a fasting-refeeding test. In a longer-term study, engineered spore administration was associated with reduced body weight and adiposity in mice with pre-existing diet-induced obesity, with semaglutide included as a positive pharmacologic benchmark. To improve its translational application, we further generated a marker-free strain that retained probiotic-relevant features of the parental strain, including gastrointestinal stress tolerance, epithelial cell adhesion, and antibiotic susceptibility. These findings provide proof of concept that engineered spore-forming bacteria may serve as a gastrointestinal peptide delivery platform and support further evaluation of this approach in disease-relevant models of metabolic dysfunction.

works.title: Dynamic populations control of Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae consortia improves chemical production
Multifunctional conductive biomimetic scaffolds combined with electrical stimulation promote neural regeneration and functional recovery after spinal cord injury
works.abstract: Abstract Electrical stimulation (ES) is an established therapeutic strategy for nerve injury that regulates neural cell behavior and promotes tissue regeneration. Furthermore, the bio-scaffolds that are sensitive to external stimuli not only influence cell behavior through their inherent properties, but also act as a medium to receive external signals and regulate cell activity. Therefore, using scaffold materials with good electroactivity combined with exogenous ES is a potentially beneficial approach for repairing spinal cord injuries (SCI). In this research, we developed a multifunctional conductive biomimetic scaffold suitable for combined electrical stimulation therapy. Firstly, a biomimetic scaffold material (GelMA) was prepared by combining patterned nanofiber with hydrogel. Then, the stromal cell-derived factor 1 labeled with 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA) (SDF-1), donepezil (DPL) and two-dimensional titanium carbide-magnesium oxide composite material (MXene-MgO) were loaded onto the surface of the scaffold. MXene-MgO, DOPA modified SDF-1 and DPL endow the scaffold material with excellent electrical conductivity, anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties, long-term stem cell recruitment function, and the ability to prevent glial scar formation during spinal cord tissue regeneration. Cell and animal experiments showed that under ES, the MXene-MgO/SDF-1/DPL scaffold can effectively enhance the activity of neural stem cells (NSCs), promote the recovery of motor function in rats, and increase the regeneration rate of new neurons. We suggest that this multi-functional bionic scaffold can provide a new treatment strategy for spinal cord injuries, and at the same time expand the application scope of auxiliary therapies such as ES.

works.title: Pharmacological ON/OFF Regulation of CAR T Cells through Estrogen Receptor-Based Stabilization and Targeted Degradation
works.abstract: Regulation of therapeutic cell response is important for safe and effective therapy, particularly for immunotherapy. Ideally, the regulators should be based on human proteins using compounds that have already been approved for human use. Regulation of protein degradation by small molecules enables fast cellular response and a small genetic footprint of genetic constructs. Here, we present a clinically compatible strategy for reversible pharmacological control of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell function using human estrogen receptor (ER)-based degron domains and FDA-approved small molecules. By fusing tamoxifen-responsive ER ligand-binding domains to CARs, we generate ligand-inducible ON-switch CARs whose stability, signaling, and effector functions are precisely controlled by 4-hydroxytamoxifen. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ER-tagged CARs can be selectively degraded using the FDA-approved ER-targeting PROTAC ARV-471, establishing a complementary OFF-switch mechanism that suppresses CAR expression and effector function. Notably, these results expand the ON-OFF switch platform for post-translational control of therapeutic proteins, offering new opportunities to improve the safety and precision of cellular immunotherapies.

works.title: Site-Selective Bioconjugations of Distinct Methionine Residues in a Protein via Reactivity-Based Reagent Control
works.abstract: The reaction of thioethers in biological macromolecules with oxaziridines enables their functionalization with moieties having utility in both basic and applied science. Exploitation of that reaction has advantages over common bioconjugations due to the relatively low abundance and weak reactivity of thioethers. Herein, we report a novel and improved route to 1-ureal piperidine,3-aryl oxaziridines that enables the preparation of bioconjugation reagents that are either electronically activated or deactivated. We leveraged the differential reactivities of the oxaziridine reagents and engineered methionine residues in distinct environments within a therapeutically relevant antibody fragment (Fab) to effect site-selective bioconjugations. We capitalized on this novel means of kinetic resolution to effect dual functionalization of a HER2-targeted Fab with distinct fluorophores for imaging receptor internalization. This work broadens the scope of what is possible in bioconjugations of thioethers and demonstrates that site-selective bioconjugations of the same residue at more than one site in a protein can be realized via reactivity-based reagent control.

works.title: G-Tract Length Shapes the Fate of G-Quadruplexes
works.abstract: Guanine (G)-rich DNA sequences can form unusual secondary structures known as G-quadruplexes (or G4s). The stability of these structures, whose folding is mainly driven by the formation and stacking of G-quartets, is influenced by several factors, foremost among them the nature of the sequence itself, particularly the nucleobases flanking the G-tracts, and the loops connecting them. A considerable effort has been devoted to understanding how the size, position, and composition of each loop and flanking sequences affect the stability of the resulting G4 fold. However, most of these studies have been restricted to sequences forming a three G-quartet G4 core. To better understand how the length of the G-tracts (from three to five Gs) and loops (from one to seven nucleotides) act in concert, we studied a set of 261 different sequences covering different possible combinations. A systematic biophysical analysis suggests that sequences with longer G-tracts tend to form more stable G4s, but also a mixture of species; it further shows that loop composition and position also influence the topology and stability of the resulting G4s. Collectively, this work provides an unprecedented view on how G4-forming sequences fold upon themselves and of the structural features that govern the stability of the resulting G4s.

works.title: Functional Characterization and Application of Yarrowia lipolytica YlYxc1 for Enhanced Production of Sphingoid Bases
works.abstract: Long-chain bases (LCBs; sphingoid bases), derived from ceramide metabolism, are valuable sphingolipid intermediates for industrial applications. Here, we functionally characterized a putative ceramidase from Yarrowia lipolytica (YlYxc1) and evaluated its potential to enhance LCB production. YlYxc1 contains a conserved alkaline ceramidase motif with seven transmembrane helices and shares ~42% amino acid identity with Saccharomyces cerevisiae alkaline ceramidases ScYpc1 and ScYdc1. Despite lacking a canonical ER retention motif, YlYxc1 localized to the ER membrane. Deletion of YlYXC1 caused no major growth or lipid profile changes. Heterologous overexpression of YlYXC1 in S. cerevisiae wild-type and Scypc1Δydc1Δ strains increased phytosphingosine (PHS) production over dihydrosphingosine (DHS), mimicking ScYPC1 overexpression. In vitro activity assays using microsomal fractions from Scypc1Δydc1Δ cells expressing YlYXC1 revealed preferential hydrolysis of phytoceramide with an alkaline pH optimum. Furthermore, YlYXC1 expression in an engineered Y. lipolytica strain expressing heterologous acetyltransferases WcSLI1 and WcATF2 remarkably enhanced acetylated LCB production. Multi-copy integration of YlYXC1 into the Ylsur2Δsld1Δ strain also increased the secretory production of non-acetylated DHS. These findings establish YlYxc1 as a promising metabolic engineering target for producing value-added LCBs for pharmaceutical and cosmeceutical applications.

works.title: Issue Information
Engineered Pseudomonas putida reconfigures metabolic fluxes during muconate bioproduction from lignin-related aromatics
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Muconic acid is a versatile platform chemical that can be biologically produced from lignocellulosic substrates, including from lignin-related aromatic compounds. Pseudomonas putida has been previously engineered to convert lignin-related aromatic compounds to muconate at quantitative molar yields. This high atom efficiency requires a supplemental carbon and energy source to support bacterial growth, and central carbon metabolic efficiency and its interaction with aromatic catabolism are underexplored. Here, we applied proteomics, metabolomics, and 13 C-fluxomics to quantitatively compare central carbon and energy metabolism in wild-type P. putida KT2440 and a muconate-producing strain, P. putida CJ781. During cultivation on glucose and 4-hydroxybenzoate, CJ781 showed increased glucose uptake, reconfigured central fluxes, and increased extracellular leakage of aliphatic acids relative to wild type. These altered fluxes supported a 3-fold higher intracellular ATP concentration and a model-predicted 2.5-fold increase in apparent ATP excess over anabolic demand. Pyruvate and acetate secretion in CJ781 was mitigated by debottlenecking TCA-cycle entry via citrate synthase overexpression. Furthermore, tuned expression of the catechol dioxygenase and protocatechuate decarboxylase enabled the production of 36.3 g L -1 muconate at 1.1 g L -1 h -1 . Overall, this work reveals how P. putida redirects carbon and energy fluxes to support aromatic bioconversion for improved bioproduction from renewable feedstocks.

works.title: Giving AI a seat at the peer review table
Conjugation of a Cell-Penetrating Peptide to the Lasso Peptides Citrocin and Microcin J25 Enhances Antimicrobial Activity
works.abstract: A subset of lasso peptides function as antibiotics against Gram-negative bacteria by inhibition of the bacterial RNA polymerase (RNAP), including microcin J25 (MccJ25) and citrocin. These peptides interact with specific transporters in the inner and outer membranes of bacteria to gain access to the cytoplasm. The reliance on transporters limits the breadth of spectrum of these lasso peptide antibiotics and opens up paths to drug resistance. Here, we detail a strategy to overcome the transport limitations of lasso peptides: covalent conjugation of the lasso peptide to a cell penetrating peptide (CPP). Citrocin-CPP and MccJ25-CPP conjugates were synthesized by attaching the CPP to the loop of the lasso peptide and tested for antimicrobial activity against the ESKAPE pathogens. Citrocin-CPP and MccJ25-CPP have antimicrobial activity against all four Gram-negative ESKAPE pathogens, a broader spectrum of activity than the parent lasso peptides. Citrocin-CPP and MccJ25-CPP also exhibit more potent activity than the parent lasso peptides, with minimum inhibitory concentrations in the high nanomolar to single micromolar range. The uptake of citrocin-CPP and MccJ25-CPP was also studied in Escherichia coli revealing that the conjugates are internalized via both transporter-dependent and transporter-independent pathways.

works.title: Bioengineering strategies for prenatal therapy
Development of a Clustering-Based Screening Using Hyperspectral Imaging for High-Producing Strains in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient screening of high-producing strains from large combinatorial libraries remains an important challenge in synthetic biology. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) enables the non-destructive evaluation of microbial colonies through the simultaneous acquisition of spectral and spatial information. In this study, we developed a novel screening strategy based on the clustering analysis of HSI-derived spectral data without the need to construct training strain sets with different production levels. As a proof of concept, we evaluated this approach using Escherichia coli with differential expression of biosynthetic genes for the production of a type II polyketide secondary metabolite, 1,3,8-trihydroxyanthraquinone (AQ256). A combinatorial library was constructed in which the transcription of AQ256 biosynthetic genes (antA-I and Pl-mcat) from Photorhabdus laumondii TTO1 was controlled by the T7 promoter or its variants. Clustering analysis revealed that AQ256 accumulation was divided into statistically distinct clusters, including those enriched in high-producing strains. The highest AQ256-producing strain, AQ-6′, identified through this screening, produced 49.0 mg L−1 in LB medium, which increased to 89.2 mg L−1 after optimizing cultivation conditions. Furthermore, proteomic analysis indicated that the increased expression of AntD/AntE, responsible for polyketide chain elongation, was associated with enhanced production. These results demonstrate that clustering based on HSI-derived spectral data enables the screening of high-producing strains without the need to prepare training data labeled according to production levels in advance and provides a useful strategy for enhancing type-II polyketide synthase-derived metabolite production.

works.title: Targeted flavour development in chocolate: omics-driven insights into cocoa fermentation
works.abstract: Cocoa fermentation is the critical microbially driven process that transforms the genetic potential of cocoa beans into the complex flavour precursors essential for high-quality chocolate. Despite its importance, fermentation remains highly variable and poorly controlled, representing a major bottleneck in the production of premium chocolate. This review explores how advanced multi-omics approaches are improving our understanding of cocoa fermentation and flavour formation by linking microbial ecology, metabolite production and sensory outcomes. It highlights the transition of cocoa fermentation from a traditional practice towards a predictive, controllable biotechnological process. Such advances pave the way for the development of tailored starter cultures, optimised fermentation processes, and ultimately, consistent production of targeted flavour development in chocolates with enhanced quality and market value.

works.title: Yeast Metabolic Engineering for Carotenoid Biosynthesis: Hosts, Pathways, Strategies, and Perspectives
works.abstract: Abstract Carotenoids are versatile natural pigments with potent antioxidant, anti-cancer, and anti-inflammatory activities, making them valuable ingredients in cosmetics, animal feed, and pharmaceuticals. While traditionally sourced from plants, algae, and microorganisms, conventional extraction methods struggle to meet the rising market demand for natural products. With the rapid advancement of synthetic biology, microbial fermentation has emerged as a scalable and efficient alternative for carotenoid production. This review paper examines four promising yeast platformsPhaffia rhodozyma, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Yarrowia lipolytica, and Komagataella phaffiifor the production of carotenoids. We systematically outline key modification strategies for the de novo biosynthetic process of carotenoids, primarily including heterologous pathway adaptation, precursor supply enhancement, protein engineering of rate-limiting enzymes, subcellular compartmentalization, and optimization of the fermentation process. Furthermore, we compare the inherent limitations of each yeast chassis and discuss potential solutions to overcome production bottlenecks, thereby providing a strategic roadmap for future strain and process development in support of industrial-scale microbial carotenoid production.

works.title: In Vivo Continuous Evolution Systems: Overview, Principles and Applications
works.abstract: Abstract Traditional in vitro directed evolution is constrained by discrete workflows, high labor demands, and separation from native cellular contexts. In vivo continuous evolution systems overcome these limitations by enabling autonomous and targeted mutagenesis coupled with cellular proliferation. This review outlines the key parts of these systems, including elevated mutation rates (10−5−10−4 substitutions per base), orthogonality, and autonomy. We classify current platforms into some categories: phage-assisted continuous evolution, error-prone polymerase-based DNA replication systems, reverse transcription-driven mutagenesis systems, and deaminase-fusion transcription-coupled mutagenesis systems, detailing their mechanisms, optimization strategies, and applications. Finally, we address technical bottlenecks and emerging directions, including AI-driven component design, automated platforms, expanded host compatibility, and broadened industrial applications, providing a roadmap for advancing continuous evolution technology.

works.title: Engineering adaptive polysaccharide biomaterials: integrated biotechnology framework for regenerative medicine
works.abstract: Natural polysaccharides are versatile building blocks for regenerative biomaterials because of their structural diversity, generally favorable biocompatibility and biodegradability, chemical tunability, and capacity for biologically relevant interactions. Advances in biotechnology and materials engineering have expanded their role from primarily structural matrices to multifunctional platforms that can influence cellular, immune, and biochemical processes during tissue repair. This review presents an integrated biological engineering framework linking polysaccharide source and molecular architecture with extraction and purification, chemical functionalization, crosslinking, advanced fabrication, biological recognition, and translational performance. Particular emphasis is placed on structure-function relationships, stereospecific glycan-receptor interactions, immune-instructive biomaterials, protein-mediated cell-material interactions, microbiome-responsive systems, and emerging artificial intelligence-assisted approaches for biomaterial design. The importance of material purity is also critically considered, particularly the potential for residual endotoxin contamination to confound interpretation of immunomodulatory responses and compromise reproducibility. Representative applications in skin, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, neural, and other regenerative systems illustrate how material composition, scaffold architecture, biofunctionalization, and manufacturing strategy collectively influence biological performance. Finally, challenges associated with scalable manufacturing, batch-to-batch reproducibility, sterilization, storage stability, quality control, regulatory translation, and clinical implementation are examined. By integrating molecular design, biological mechanisms, fabrication, and translational requirements, this review provides engineering principles for the development of adaptive polysaccharide biomaterials and identifies priorities for advancing reproducible and clinically translatable regenerative technologies.

works.title: High-throughput mass spectrometry-based metabolomics for large-scale population studies: technical barriers and recent innovations
works.abstract: Large-scale metabolomic studies are needed to identify and validate biomarkers for their successful translation in emerging population health and precision medicine initiatives. Yet, untargeted mass spectrometry (MS)-based metabolomics remains hampered by low sample throughput, limited coverage, complicated data processing, poor standardization, and high operating costs. These challenges also contribute to a reproducibility crisis, with most reported biomarkers not independently replicated, given variations in study designs, sample workup protocols, instrumental methods, and data pre-processing workflows. This review will focus on new advances in high-throughput MS platforms and computational software with emerging artificial intelligence/machine learning tools that are scalable, faster, and less prone to error. Recent progress to improve data harmonization in population-level metabolomic, lipidomic, and exposomic studies (n > 1000) will also be discussed. This will include strategies to correct for long-term batch effects, improve metabolite identification, and derive biochemical insights into disease mechanisms when integrated with multi-omic studies.

works.title: Editorial overview: Environmental Biotechnology in 2026: challenges, opportunities, and new frontiers
A Biocompatible Cu(I)-Catalyzed Click Chemistry Framework for Long-Term Cell Tracking
works.abstract: Cellular immunotherapies have transformed oncologic treatment in recent years, yet the inability to monitor cell migration post-transfusion remains a significant barrier to their development. Here, we explore the feasibility of a non-invasive cell-tracking method utilizing Cu(I)-catalyzed click chemistry in which cells are first labeled with alkynes and, after 1-2 weeks, are selectively targeted via an azide-conjugated fluorescent probe. We developed Click1, a novel tris-Cu-chelating azide capable of a rapid, robust click reaction directly on live cell surfaces with minimal cytotoxicity. When paired with Click1, two distinct alkyne-labeling reagents, N-(4-pentynoyl)-mannosamine-tetraacylated (Ac4ManNAl) and propargyl choline, were capable of detecting human T cells for over two weeks. Our findings elucidate the metabolic turnover of biochemical handles in primary immune cells, providing a potential framework for long-term cell tracking in immunotherapies.

works.title: A Modular Optogenetic Split-Small GTPase Platform Reveals Long-Range RhoA Signaling
works.abstract: Small GTPases are critical regulators of cellular processes such as cell migration. However, no generalizable method exists for directly controlling their activity with subcellular precision, limiting the ability to dissect long-range signaling effects. To address this, we pair fragmented small GTPases with improved light-inducible dimerization (iLID) domains, optimizing for low dark-state background and efficient light-induced reassembly, affording spLIT-small GTPases. Demonstrating modularity, we control filopodia formation (spLIT-Cdc42), cell movement (spLIT-Rac1), and membrane retraction (spLIT-RhoA) with subcellular precision. Applying this platform to long-range signaling, we provide the first demonstration that localized RhoA activation is sufficient to drive membrane retraction at the opposite cell pole, with a directional dependence set by actin cytoskeleton polarization, a result inaccessible to global perturbations used previously. These results suggest a mechanism for coordinated establishment of cell polarity and highlight spLIT-small GTPases as a versatile platform for the direct, spatial control of small GTPase signaling in living cells.

works.title: Enhanced Production of Nitrogenase Components NifU and NifH in Nicotiana benthamiana through Co-expression with Bacterioferritin A
works.abstract: Abstract Generating crops that utilize atmospheric nitrogen rather than soil nitrogen requires the transfer of nitrogenase structural genes together with genes required for the biosynthesis of nitrogenase iron−sulfur cofactors. Scaffold proteins, such as NifU, are the starting point of nitrogenase cofactor assembly. While NifU has been successfully produced in plants, its optimal production was achieved with iron supplementation in the nutrient solution. This suggests a faulty connection with the endogenous iron trafficking network, indicating the need for specific elements targeting iron to NifU. Here, we identify bacterioferritin A (BfrA) as an iron donor to NifU. Co-expression with BfrA increases NifU production in Nicotiana benthamiana, leading to doubling the production of NifH, a nitrogenase structural protein that is also required for the synthesis of more complex nitrogenase cofactors. This work underscores the importance of transferring metal delivery systems alongside metalloproteins when engineering heterologous systems.

Chemogenetic activation of mitochondria counteracts the Warburg effect in tumor cells
