Characterization of Chromone Biosynthetic Pathway Reveals a Noncanonical Mode of Fungal Polyketide Cyclization
works.abstract: Fungal nonreducing polyketide synthases (NRPKSs) produce therapeutically and ecologically important aromatic polyketides. The product template (PT) domain of fungal NRPKSs catalyzes the regioselective aldol cyclization of the reactive poly-β-ketone chain during polyketide maturation and is essential for product fidelity of the NRPKSs. Herein, we discovered the fungal NRPKS MecA of which the polyketide cyclization steps do not involve a functional PT domain. MecA is encoded in the biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) responsible for the formation of 5-hydroxy-7-methoxy-2,3-dimethylchromone (1) from the biocontrol fungus Trichoderma afroharzianum T22. Heterologous expression and in vitro enzymatic assays fully established a biosynthetic pathway of 1 that involves three enzymes: MecA, dehydratase MecB, and methyltransferase MecC. The PT domain of MecA does not contain the conserved catalytic histidine that is essential for aldol cyclization activity. Consistent with the predicted inactive PT domain, MecA was demonstrated to catalyze a C1-C6 Claisen condensation as the first cyclization step of the pentaketide precursor, instead of the canonical aldol cyclization. Reconstitution of dissected MecA domains further demonstrated that the activity of MecA was not affected when the PT domain was removed. A Claisen Cyclase (CLC) domain that typically catalyzes Claisen cyclization in NRPKSs is also absent in MecA, implying the observed C1-C6 cyclization step is catalyzed by the remaining domains. This work contributes to the diversity of NRPKS cyclization chemistry and enables further genome mining and engineering of NRPKSs that may lead to biosynthesis of new aromatic polyketides.

works.title: Translation of in vivo CAR-T in China
Engineering GFPuv Reporters for Visual Screening across Filamentous Fungi to Enable CRISPR Genome Editing in Aspergillus pseudoterreus
works.abstract: Abstract GFPuv is a UV-excitable fluorescent reporter that enables rapid monitoring of gene expression, particularly in microbial systems. However, its application in filamentous fungi remains limited. Here, we evaluated GFPuv variants and identified one that performs robustly across Aspergillus species and the yeast Yarrowia lipolytica. Under UV illumination, transformed green fluorescent colonies can be visualized without colony dissection or microscopy, significantly simplifying screening. CRISPR-based genome editing has not been previously established in Aspergillus pseudoterreus. By integrating the optimized GFPuv reporter into a transformation and selection system, we established, to our knowledge, the first CRISPR knockout platform in this species. Targeted disruption of the genes pyrG, CAD, and PrID505606 validated the platform. PCR and Sanger sequencing confirmed that GFPuv-positive colonies were true mutants, while loss-of-function phenotypes of pyrG and CAD further supported platform reliability. This work establishes GFPuv as a rapid, microscopy-independent screening tool in select fungi and provides a foundational CRISPR framework for engineering A. pseudoterreus.

works.title: Unraveling the proteome of Escherichia coli during L-phenylalanine production in a scale-down bioreactor
works.abstract: Large-scale industrial bioprocesses are characterized by spatial and temporal inhomogeneities that expose microorganisms to fluctuating bioprocess conditions. These gradients can strongly influence cellular physiology, thereby affecting bioprocess robustness and product formation. Although phenotypic population heterogeneity under such conditions has been described, the underlying protein-level mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, the impact of environmental fluctuations on the proteome of an L-phenylalanine producing Escherichia coli strain was investigated. Samples were collected from cultivations in a well-mixed stirred-tank bioreactor and a two-compartment bioreactor operated at mean hydraulic residence times of τ = 103s and τ = 404s. Global proteome patterns were analyzed using principal component analysis (PCA), followed by differential protein abundance analysis and functional interpretation by gene ontology (GO) enrichment and clusters of orthologous groups (COG)-based analysis. PCA identified residence time in the bypass as the dominant factor shaping proteome variation. Prolonged exposure to limiting conditions at τ = 404s led to a distinct clustering of proteome profiles, clearly separated from both the stirred-tank bioreactor and the shorter residence time condition. GO enrichment analysis revealed increased abundance of proteins associated with stress response during the batch and product formation phases, and proteins related to cell communication during biomass production. Consistently, COG-based analysis showed a shift from growth- and production-associated proteins toward maintenance and stress adaptation in cells from the two-compartment bioreactor, with this shift becoming more pronounced at longer residence times.

works.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
works.abstract: Abstract Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf . In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf , Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet ; CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

works.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
works.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

works.title: Characterization of methylxanthine production in metabolically engineered Pseudomonas putida
works.abstract: Pseudomonas putida can utilize a wide variety of carbon sources, making it a promising bacterial host for biochemical production. P. putida CBB5 is able to convert caffeine to higher value methylxanthines through a series of N- demethylation reactions. The genes responsible for the N -demethylation of caffeine, ndmABCDE , have been previously isolated and expressed in the model organism Escherichia coli due to its robust set of genetic engineering tools. However, expression in the host of origin is preferred, and recent studies have expanded and consolidated the genetic toolkit of P. putida KT2440. This work aims to further develop and optimize the available tools for P. putida KT2440 through the construction and characterization of an expression plasmid and demonstration of its utility using N -demethylase genes. We developed the IPTG-inducible expression plasmid pRC000 for use in P. putida KT2440. Functionality of the inducible system was confirmed using a green fluorescent protein assay and further characterized using a β-galactosidase assay. We observed leaky expression when expressing any gene other than gfp . We also cloned genes for the N 1 -demethylation, N 3 -demethylation, and N 7 -demethylation of methylxanthines into pRC000. Modified KT2440 strains diluted to an OD 600 of 5.0 consumed 4.924 ± 0.158 mM caffeine or 4.430 ± 0.482 mM theobromine in two hours. Strains capable of the two-step conversion of caffeine to 7-methylxanthine experienced relatively little loss of efficiency compared to those performing one-step conversion. N- demethylase mutants ndmA3 and ndmA4 , originally developed in E. coli , were also cloned in pRC000 and successfully expressed in KT2440. Cells expressing ndmA3 converted 0.956 ± 0.044 mM theophylline to 1-methylxanthine in one hour, while cells expressing ndmA4 converted 0.945 ± 0.101 mM theophylline. This study demonstrated the potential of P. putida KT2440 as a microbial host for methylxanthine production. Engineered N 1 - and N 3 -demethylase systems exhibited higher rates and generated higher product yields when expressed in P. putida compared to their E. coli counterparts.

works.title: Biophysical regulation of cell plasticity for induced neuron generation
works.abstract: Biophysical signals are key regulators of development, tissue regeneration, aging, disease pathogenesis, and cellular plasticity, yet they have received considerably less attention than biochemical cues. Defined as the capacity of cells to alter their phenotypes in response to diverse stimuli, cell plasticity has become a cornerstone of regenerative medicine, disease modeling, and pharmaceutical research. However, the robust epigenetic barriers in mature cells severely hamper cell fate conversion, and overreliance on biochemical inducers often triggers cytotoxic side effects. During development, biophysical signals can activate specialized mechanotransduction programs, which interact dynamically with biochemical signals to modulate cell fate. Cumulative studies have shown that external biophysical cues, whether used individually or in combination with chemical regulators, markedly enhance cell transition efficiency. Integrating physical and biochemical cues therefore provides a powerful paradigm for accurate cell-fate manipulation. In this review, we comprehensively summarize four mainstream biophysical strategies for generating induced neurons (iNs) in vitro: matrix stiffness/viscoelasticity, matrix topography, mechanically induced cell deformation, and non-contact physical stimulation. We further dissect the underlying mechanisms linking mechanosensitive proteins, canonical mechanotransduction pathways, and epigenetic remodeling. Overall, biophysical cue-guided cell fate conversion represents a promising strategy for generating functional neurons and other cell types, with potential applications in disease modeling, regenerative medicine, and cell-based therapies. Cell plasticity is an evolutionarily conserved biological trait, offering promising therapeutic potential for neurodegenerative diseases and neural injuries. Biophysical cues serve as powerful regulators of cell fate, acting via distinct mechanotransduction and epigenetic pathways. Combined biophysical and biochemical strategies markedly improve the efficiency and quality of induced neuron generation. Systematic screening and optimization of biophysical cues facilitate the development of novel therapeutic approaches for neurological disorders.

works.title: Bioprocess intensification of serum-free vaccinia virus production in Vero cells: a comparative study of Cell Factory and tide motion bioreactor platforms
works.abstract: Vaccinia virus (VACV) remains an important vaccine and viral-vector platform, but production in adherent cells becomes increasingly cumbersome when capacity is expanded mainly by adding planar culture units. Serum-free cultivation can further support process standardization by reducing reliance on animal-derived components and associated batch-to-batch variability. We evaluated serum-free VACV production in Vero cells using two independently operated process configurations: a conventional 10-layer Cell Factory (6,320 cm 2 growth area) and a BelloStage™-3000 tide-motion system using BelloCell® 500A vessels containing 5.5 g of BioNOC™ II macrocarriers (approximately 15,600 cm 2 manufacturer-reported surface area). The processes were compared in terms of cell expansion, endpoint infectious virus titer, nutrient behavior, cumulative infectious virus recovery, and space-time yield (STY). In the Cell Factory process, the estimated total Vero cell number increased from 5.70 × 10 7 to 2.94 × 10 8 cells, corresponding to a 5.2-fold expansion, while cell viability remained above 90%. In the BelloStage™-3000 process, the estimated total cell number increased from 8.70 × 10 7 to 1.16 × 10 9 cells, corresponding to a 13.3-fold expansion, with viability ranging from 84% to 93%. Mean final infectious virus titers were 5.75 ± 0.25 and 6.42 ± 0.14 log₁₀ TCID₅₀/mL for the Cell Factory and BelloStage™-3000 processes, respectively. Mean cumulative infectious virus yield, calculated separately for each biological replicate, was (9.39 ± 5.19) × 10 8 TCID₅₀ per replicate for the Cell Factory process and (1.35 ± 0.40) × 10 9 TCID₅₀ per replicate for the BelloStage™-3000 process, a 1.44-fold difference between the means. Corresponding mean STY values were (3.13 ± 1.73) × 10 8 and (4.51 ± 1.32) × 10 8 TCID₅₀/L/day. Glucose generally decreased during cell expansion and virus production, with transient increases after scheduled medium replacement, whereas changes in culture medium pH were modest. Under the conditions evaluated, the BelloStage™-3000 process showed a larger estimated fold expansion of Vero cells, a numerically higher mean endpoint infectious virus titer, and moderately higher cumulative infectious virus yield and STY than the Cell Factory process. The results support further evaluation of tide-motion cultivation as a laboratory-scale platform for intensified serum-free Ospa-Vaktsina production and evaluation at larger scale.

works.title: ChronoCCI decodes the chronological logic of cell-cell communication along branching single-cell trajectories
works.abstract: Abstract Cell-cell communication (CCI) drives cell-fate decisions during tissue development, yet mapping these dynamics at single-cell resolution remains a challenge. While existing single-cell tools infer static signaling networks or map linear trajectories, they fail to capture the continuous, asynchronous coordination of pathways at multilineage branching points. Consequently, identifying the precise chronological timing of interactions and specific molecular triggers remains a major challenge. To resolve this, we introduce ChronoCCI, an automated Python framework that aligns consensus ligand-receptor networks directly with multi-trajectory Markov chain dynamics from CellRank. By modeling continuous expression trends across branching lineages via fate-weighted smoothing, ChronoCCI reconstructs the chronological cascade of tissue signaling on a shared time axis, tracking active cell types at the peak of each molecular wave. Crucially, ChronoCCI incorporates snoop_py, a screening algorithm leveraging chronological Mean Absolute Error (MAE) scoring to automatically isolate highly asymmetric lineage-specific signaling gatekeepers at developmental bifurcations. Validated on a human peripheral blood mononuclear cell dataset, ChronoCCI autonomously maps the temporal dynamics of myeloid maturation. It successfully prioritizes the GNAI2 - C5AR1 phagocytic checkpoint and the late-stage SELPLG - ESAM vascular rolling axis as highly asymmetric chronological triggers selectively retained along distinct lineages. Requiring zero prior biological assumptions, ChronoCCI provides a powerful tool to dissect intercellular cross-talk in developmental, regenerative, and pathological tissue atlases.

works.title: Improving PROTAC-Mediated Degradation in Mouse Models: BRD9 as a Case Study
works.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) have emerged as powerful chemical tools and therapeutics, yet their translation from preclinical models to humans remains inconsistent. Here, we systematically evaluate the activity of BRD9-targeting PROTACs in human and mouse systems to elucidate a key limitation in preclinical studies. Widely used CRBN- and VHL-recruiting degraders, including dBRD9 and VZ185, exhibit markedly reduced potency in mouse cells despite high sequence conservation of BRD9. Mechanistic interrogation reveals that species-specific differences in E3 ligases, particularly the Crbn I391 residue and structural variations in VHL, likely impair productive ternary complex formation. Expression of human CRBN or VHL, or introduction of the CrbnI391V mutation, increases degradation potency in mouse cells. Importantly, in vivo studies demonstrate enhanced BRD9 degradation in CrbnI391V mice using clinically relevant degraders. These findings highlight a critical barrier in PROTAC evaluation and establish humanized E3 ligase models as tools for more accurate assessment of on-target efficacy and toxicity.

works.title: Production of Polyclonal Mixes of Full-Size IgG Antibodies in Plants Using a Two-Viral-Vector System
works.abstract: Abstract Plants are cost-effective bioreactors to produce recombinant proteins for many different biotechnological applications, and plant virus-derived vectors are frequently used to improve yield and shorten production times. Antibodies, the products of vertebrate immune systems, display unsurpassed features in terms of affinity, selectivity, and avidity for their cognate antigens. However, antibody size and heteromultimeric structures make their expression in plants difficult, particularly when employing viral vectors, which typically exhibit cargo restrictions. Here, we have worked on a dual vector system based on potato virus X (PVX) and tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) to produce polyclonal mixes of recombinant antibodies in Nicotiana benthamiana plants. In this system, the heavy and light chains of the different antibodies that compose the polyclonal mix are expressed, respectively, through defective PVX and TMV vectors. Importantly, to avoid antibody chain shuffling in the polyclonal mix, each pair of PVX-TMV vectors that express the cognate heavy and light chains of each monoclonal antibody is inoculated into the plant tissue using a single Agrobacterium tumefaciens clone co-transformed with two mini-binary plasmids with compatible replication origins, in which the viral vectors are cloned. Both viral vectors lack their coat proteins, which contributes to better coupling of the cell-to-cell movement of the two vectors. In addition, the recombinant antibodies are exported to the apoplast of infiltrated tissues from where the polyclonal mix can be easily extracted and directly used for many applications with no further purification. Using this dual vector system, we have successfully produced inN. benthamiana a polyclonal mix of recombinant antibodies that efficiently bind the nucleocapsid protein and two independent epitopes of the spike protein from SARS-CoV-2.

works.title: Biofoundry Data Interoperability Requires Community Action
works.abstract: Abstract Biofoundries are automated laboratory platforms that execute design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles at scale, generating vast experimental datasets with the potential to accelerate biological discovery and grow the bioeconomy. Independent development across institutions has produced incompatible data formats and no agreed schema linking experimental metadata across cycles or between facilities, preventing aggregation for cross-institutional validation, machine learning, and reproducibility. Neither the international consortium nor the formal standards body with the mandate to act has done so, leaving an organizational gap that no technical solution has yet resolved. Closing the gap will necessitate three sequential steps: a community-driven working group to establish minimum data standards and schema, a funded international pilot cohort to test and refine them, and downstream formalization through established standards bodies. Community consensus must run ahead of, not concurrently with, formal standardization. Both the Bermuda Principles and the Protein Data Bank demonstrate that global scientific communities can establish binding data norms without a mandate, through collective agreement or through incentive structures that make compliance desirable.

works.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing
works.abstract: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization. Human Argonaute is repurposed for RNA editing.

works.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity
works.abstract: Microorganisms have the potential to deliver growth-promoting benefits to plants and crops; however, to be useful in a field setting, their gene expression should be programmable and restricted to specific plant hosts and conditions. Here, using O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) as a model compound, we establish noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a tool for plant-based control of associated microbial activity. We use genetic code expansion to engineer OMY-dependent control of protein synthesis in the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis. Engineered B. subtilis strains express an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pair that, upon provision of OMY, results in suppression of in-frame amber stop codons in target transcripts. We engineer Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to biosynthesize OMY, showing that plant-derived OMY can stimulate gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. This demonstrates that inducible and tissue-specific expression of a single biosynthetic enzyme by the plant enables on-demand control over microbial activity, establishing ncAAs as a tool for programming plant-microorganism partnerships.

works.title: Yeast-based biosensors for detection of rare earth elements
works.abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) are vital to modern technologies due to their unique chemical properties and diverse industrial applications. Detecting various REEs at low concentrations within complex matrices requires highly sensitive and selective methods. We report the development of an intensiometric biosensor that exploits the conformational change of lanmodulin (LanM) upon REE binding. LanM was inserted into the superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP), creating a chimeric biosensor in which LanM functions as the input domain controlling fluorescence output. Computationally designed linker libraries connecting LanM to two sfGFP insertion sites were screened using yeast display coupled to flow cytometry, yielding constructs that exhibited fluorescence enhancement in response to REEs. The whole-cell biosensor demonstrated instantaneous response, a detection limit of low micromolar concentration, and high selectivity for REEs over alkaline earth and transition metals. The yeast-based intensiometric biosensor provides a versatile platform for high-throughput screening and optimization of LanM variants with tailored specificity and sensitivity toward different REEs.

works.title: Structurally informed metabolite measurements with ion mobility-mass spectrometry
works.abstract: Although ion mobility-mass spectrometry (IM-MS) is no longer a new technology, new developments in instrumentation and resources for structurally informed measurements are enabling the use of IM-MS in emerging metabolomic applications. Once limited by experimental measurements, the growth of machine-learning strategies to predict collision cross-section values is rapidly increasing the coverage of IM-MS information in metabolite databases. IM-MS instrumentation capable of high-resolution separations is bringing new depth to the level of structural annotation that can be achieved, while creative strategies to combine IM-MS with complementary analytical or chemical methods are further leveraging its ability to resolve small molecule isomers and isobars. This brief review highlights the recent developments of IM-MS for metabolomics with a focus on applications to mass spectrometry imaging, rapid multi-omics, and single-cell analyses.

A Synthetic Promoter Library Spanning a Wide Dynamic Range for Metabolic Pathway Engineering in Zymomonas mobilis
works.abstract: Abstract The limited availability of reliable genetic tools has hindered the engineering of Zymomonas mobilis, a promising bacterium for the sustainable bioproduction of commodity chemicals. Here, we present a synthetic promoter library that enables high-resolution control of gene expression in Z. mobilis. We constructed and characterized 29 promoters spanning the broadest dynamic range reported for this organism to date, and 25 were identified with expression levels higher than the previously reported strongest native constitutive promoter, Pgap, including some up to 15-fold higher. Additionally, a set of strong heterologous and synthetic transcriptional terminators that effectively insulate genetic cassettes was validated in Z. mobilis. Promoters were stable under both aerobic and anaerobic conditions, highlighting their robustness in industrially relevant conditions. Surprisingly, all of the promoters identified contained non-canonical promoter element sequences that adhered poorly to the proposed consensus sequences. The promoter library and terminators were integrated into the Type IIS-based, hierarchical start−stop assembly system, facilitating high-throughput construction of multi-cistronic designs. We demonstrate their utility through the rapid construction, testing, and optimization of a 2,3-butanediol biosynthetic pathway. This resource substantially expands the accessible expression space for metabolic engineering in Z. mobilis, supporting precise tuning of multi-step pathways and genetic circuits.

works.title: Orchestrating polyketide synthase-derived aldehyde metabolism for Streptomyces biomanufacturing
works.abstract: Advances in metabolic engineering have enabled the integration of diverse non-native reactions into microbial hosts, providing sustainable alternatives to petrochemical manufacturing. We previously developed a modular polyketide synthase (PKS)-based platform in Streptomyces albus for producing 17 diols, amino alcohols, and hydroxy acids. In this platform, terminal thioester reductases (TRs) release aldehyde intermediates that are subsequently converted by post-PKS enzymes to control product chemistry. Here we found that PKS-TR strains accumulated hundreds of genome-wide single-nucleotide variants, including missense mutations on conserved PKS and TR residues leading to impaired enzyme activity. Based on the hypothesis of aldehyde toxicity, we coupled TR catalysis with downstream alcohol dehydrogenases (ADHs) through gene co-integration or PKS-TR-ADH fusion to limit aldehyde accumulation. These strategies reduced genomic variability and increased diol production, reaching a total diol titer of 14.2 g/L in bioreactors, including 10.8 g/L 1,3-butanediol. Extending this approach, engineered strains incorporating PKS-TR co-integration with transaminases or the padA aldehyde dehydrogenase achieved 79% higher total amino alcohol titers and 145% higher 2-methyl-3-hydroxyhexanoic acid titer than previous reports, while eliminating diol byproducts from the optimized hydroxy acid pathway. These results establish TR-mediated aldehyde release as a programmable branch point and orchestrated downstream catalysis as a general strategy for improving the stability, productivity, and selectivity of PKS-based Streptomyces biomanufacturing.

works.title: Development of a Chlorella-based serum-free culture formulation for HaCaT cells with metabolic and attachment support
works.abstract: Abstract Background Fetal bovine serum (FBS) provides diverse soluble and extracellular functions that are difficult to reproduce in serum-free culture, particularly for anchorage-dependent cells. This study aimed to develop a microalgae-based serum-free formulation for HaCaT keratinocytes by evaluating microalgae-derived soluble components, selected culture supplements, and an attachment-supporting component. Results Among low-molecular-weight fractions (LFs) prepared from green Chlorella vulgaris and white and yellow Auxenochlorella protothecoides , green C. vulgaris LF produced the highest MTT-derived metabolic activity. Supplementation with insulin-transferrin-selenium, albumin, and ascorbic acid, designated as the supplement mixture (SM), further increased the MTT response, but the resulting LF + SM formulation did not maintain observable cell attachment after passage. Addition of fish gelatin to SM generated SMG, and the resulting LF + SMG formulation improved post-passage cell retention. Under standardized reseeding conditions, direct viable-cell counting showed that LF + SMG supported cell expansion through four consecutive passages, reaching 7.84 cumulative population doublings by P4. Hoechst-normalized F-actin-associated fluorescence was also maintained during later passages under LF + SMG conditions. Conclusions The final LF + SMG formulation supported post-passage cell retention and HaCaT cell expansion through four consecutive passages by integrating microalgae-derived soluble components, selected culture supplements, and attachment support. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of a Chlorella -based serum-free formulation that provides metabolic and attachment support for serial HaCaT cell culture.

works.title: Chemical and Genetically Encoded Strategies for Spatiotemporal Control of Lipid Generation in Living Cells
works.abstract: Mammalian cells synthesize thousands of distinct lipids, and lipid metabolism fundamentally influences signaling in both homeostatic and disease states. Despite considerable interest in the biological functions of diverse lipid species, direct study of their effects in biological systems has historically been limited by a lack of methods to modulate discrete lipid species with precise spatiotemporal control. Several efforts in lipid chemical biology focus on the development of technologies to generate individual lipid species with spatial and temporal control in living cells. Emerging strategies are enabling the on-demand generation of lipids in response to various stimuli. In this Perspective, we discuss three mechanistic approaches for controlled lipid generation: light-triggered production of lipids from modified precursors, orthogonal chemical release, and triggerable chemoenzymatic or genetically encoded enzymatic generation of lipids. We highlight the strengths and weaknesses of each platform, and we outline the design strategies that will shape the next generation of tools.

works.title: AMY-SA-XGBoost: A Machine Learning Model to Predict Amylase Specific Activity
works.abstract: Abstract Amylase is an important enzyme preparation, and its enzyme activity directly determines its catalytic efficiency in starch hydrolysis. However, current experimental methods for determining amylase specific activity are time-consuming and costly, and experimentally measured specific activity data are sparse and noisy, with limited experimental data currently available. We developed AMY-SA-XGBoost, a machine learning-based approach for predicting amylase specific activity. We systematically constructed a high-quality dataset comprising 178 samples suitable for studying amylase catalytic efficiency by collecting and screening amylase activity data from enzyme databases and literature. The XGBoost-based model exhibited strong predictive performance for amylase activity, with an R2 of 0.9378 and an RMSE of 0.4329. The AMY-SA-XGBoost can capture specific activity changes in mutated enzymes and identify amino acid residues with substantial impact on specific activity. In addition, we screened 14 amylase mutants with the highest predicted increases in specific activity and experimentally validated each mutant. Experimental results confirm that AMY-SA-XGBoost accurately predicts the specific activity of amylase mutants based on their amino acid sequences, successfully identifying variants with higher activity. Among the tested mutants, S359N demonstrated the most significant improvement, achieving a specific activity of 9573 ± 21.30 U/mg. This work provides both theoretical foundation and practical insights for enhancing the catalytic efficiency of amylase in pharmaceutical and food industry applications.

works.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Beyond the obvious pocket
Tryptoline stereoprobe elaboration identifies inhibitors of the GRPEL1–HSPA9 complex
works.abstract: Activity-based protein profiling has identified hundreds of human proteins from diverse classes that react at cysteine residues with stereochemically defined electrophilic compounds (stereoprobes). The structure-activity relationships underlying these stereoprobe-protein interactions, however, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the protein interaction landscape of tryptoline acrylamide stereoprobes can be profoundly altered by structural modifications distal to the acrylamide reactive group. Most stereoprobe liganding events occurred at nonorthosteric sites and evaded assignment by the machine learning-based cofolding model Boltz-2, which instead tended to misplace stereoprobes in orthosteric pockets (an outcome we term 'orthostery burnout'). We found that stereoprobes reacting with C124 in the nucleotide exchange factor GRPEL1 disrupt interactions with the mitochondrial HSP70 chaperone HSPA9/mortalin, leading to impairments in mitochondrial protein import and mitophagy induction. Our results highlight tryptoline acrylamides as a versatile source of covalent ligands targeting nonorthosteric sites on proteins, including tool compounds that perturb the mitochondrial HSP70 chaperone system.

works.title: A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5′-monophosphate from adenosine
works.abstract: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

works.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information
Tn7 Integration Efficiently Introduces Gene Expression Cassettes into a Gut-Native Escherichia coli Strain
works.abstract: Abstract Native bacteria are strains isolated from the host and often require greater development and optimization of genetic manipulation tools than lab-adapted strains. We have previously shown that the native murine Escherichia coli strain EcAZ-1, which colonizes the conventional mouse gut long term, is genetically tractable, and the engineered strain can elicit physiological effects while residing in the mouse gut. Given the interest in using EcAZ-1 and other native E. coli as a chassis for heterologous gene expression in the mouse gut, researchers need more efficient tools to rapidly and reliably introduce heterologous gene expression into the strain. Here, we demonstrate that a gene expression cassette can be integrated into the EcAZ-1 genome with high efficiency using the site-specific Tn7 transposon. Furthermore, we demonstrate that EcAZ-1 modified to express sfGFP using this method stably engrafts in the gut of conventional mouse. Taken together, Tn7-mediated integration is an effective method for stably introducing genetic cassettes into the native murine strain EcAZ-1 for expression in the mouse gut.

works.title: De novo biosynthesis of the plant-derived aloe-emodin in Aspergillus nidulans via artificial pathway assembly and temporal flux control
Late-stage large extracellular vesicles reprogram CHO cell metabolism in a glutamine-dependent mode and promote antibody-productivity to cell-growth tradeoff
works.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are mediators of intercellular communication, yet their impact on Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cell physiology and bioprocess performance remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether small EVs (sEVs) and large EVs (LgEVs) that accumulate during fed-batch and perfusion cultures modulate CHO cell growth, metabolism, apoptosis, and monoclonal antibody (mAb) production. EVs isolated from early- and late-stage cultures were added to fresh CHO cultures grown with or without glutamine supplementation. Only LgEVs had a significant impact. Late-stage LgEVs markedly altered CHO-cell behavior, reducing cell proliferation, increasing apoptosis under glutamine-limited conditions, and substantially enhancing mAb productivity in a dose-dependent manner. Glutamine supplementation largely alleviated the growth-inhibitory and pro-apoptotic effects of LgEVs while preserving their positive impact on productivity, suggesting that glutamine mitigated the EV-mediated stress without affecting the productivity enhancement. Metabolic analyses revealed increased glucose consumption, an enhanced glutamine-dependent shift between glycine and alanine overflow metabolism, and remodeling of amino-acid utilization. Metabolic flux analysis further demonstrated enhanced glycolytic overflow and increased reliance on amino acid-supported anaplerosis. Conversely, selective removal of LgEVs from perfusion medium significantly improved cell expansion without reducing antibody production, supporting an inhibitory role for late-stage LgEVs. These LgEVs were enriched in let-7 family miRNAs and miR-21, consistent with RNAseq analyses demonstrating stress-associated enrichment of these miRNAs in CHO EVs and with functional studies showing that let-7a and miR-21 reduce CHO-cell growth. Together, these observations suggest that selective miRNA loading contributes to the growth, metabolic, and productivity phenotypes elicited by late-stage LgEVs. Our findings identify LgEVs in CHO-K1 can act as endogenous regulators of CHO-cell physiology thus deserving attention for optimizing high-density fed-batch and perfusion biomanufacturing processes.

works.title: Single Staphylococcus aureus SauUSI restriction enzyme motors fragment methylated DNA
works.abstract: SauUSI is a dimeric, ATP-dependent type IV restriction enzyme that protects Staphylococcus aureus by cleaving nonself DNA containing 5-methylcytosine or 5-hydroxymethylcytosine. Using biophysical, single-molecule and nanopore sequencing methods, we show that 5-methylcytosine recognition first induces ATP-driven unidirectional translocation by one helicase-like subunit, displacing its target recognition domain (TRD). In half of events, the partner TRD can then bind the liberated modified site, stabilizing a growing DNA loop. On symmetrically methylated DNA, looping is more frequent and both motors can engage in bidirectional loop translocation. Cleavage occurs stochastically throughout translocation but events that increase dwell time such as rebinding methylated sites elevate the chance of cleavage. Interactions with other SauUSI dimers or protein roadblocks influence cleavage distributions but are not required for nuclease activation. While the first cleavages principally generate 1-nt 3' overhangs or blunt ends, multiple binding-translocation-cleavage cycles by individual enzymes ultimately fragment the modified nonself DNA, neutralizing its threat.

works.title: Structural variant detection across sequencing technologies
works.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are a major source of genomic diversity, yet their discovery remains challenging due to repetitive genomic contexts, alignment ambiguity and the trade-off between sequencing cost and read length. Here we introduce HitSV, which implements repetitiveness- and signature-density-aware breakpoint recognition coupled with precise haplotype-resolved local assembly, thereby enabling base-resolution SV reconstruction and genotyping in various sequencing technologies. On the HG002 benchmark, HitSV achieved 15-72% (long read), 10-36% (short read) and 12% (hybrid sequencing), respectively, higher genotype F1 scores than state-of-the-art SV callers. Applied to the 1KGP phase 4 cohort, HitSV expanded the SV callset by 31.5%, substantially reshaping allele-frequency landscapes. In a large Chinese long-read cohort, HitSV uncovered tandem-repeat-mobile-element composite arrays as a prevalent, multi-allelic class of complex SVs, highlighting composite repeat architectures as an important and previously underrecognized contributor to human structural variation.

works.title: Explotation of 3D-printed bone scaffolds architecture: a Design of Experiment (DOE) and computational fluid dynamic (CFD)-finite element method (FEM) framework ranking study
works.abstract: In silico analysis of tissue engineering products is an efficient tool to predict and design the optimal substitute in developing scaffolds. The primary objective of this study is to computationally rank a set of twelve predefined internal architectures of PCL polymer-based 3D-printed bone scaffolds and identify the best-performing candidate, considering two essential aspects: (i) the magnitude of fluid-induced mechanical stimuli, namely wall shear stress (WSS) and pressure gradients, which are established biophysical regulators of osteogenic differentiation and proliferation, and (ii) the scaffold’s structural integrity and resistance to mechanical failure (quantified via Von Mises stress distribution), thereby avoiding stress-shielding and localized collapse under compressive loading. Initially, the scaffold designs were created according to specified design requirements, including form, the presence or absence of a central connection, and the profile type, including round, square, and octagonal, using a computerized drawing and planning tool. A total of 12 models were ultimately generated, using the Design of Experiments (DOE) methodology to thoroughly examine the mechanical characteristics and conduct simulations for perfusion bioreactor testing. In the second phase, the mechanical behavior of the scaffolds was analyzed under two distinct physiological loading scenarios using a one-way decoupled FEM approach. In the first scenario, fluid-induced tractions (pressure and wall shear stress) obtained from the CFD solution were mapped onto the scaffold surfaces via one-way FSI, representing the mechanical stimuli exerted by the perfused culture medium under bioreactor perfusion conditions; this scenario was used for the primary parametric study and ranking of the twelve scaffold designs. In the second, separate scenario, a uniaxial compression simulation was performed, in which a compressive pressure load of 0.5 MPa was applied to the scaffold’s top surface with the bottom surface fully constrained, representing the real-life mechanical pressure experienced by the scaffold during daily physiological activity. In addition, a dynamic analysis was conducted to ascertain the fluid pressure distribution, velocity profile, and shear stress of the scaffold walls by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis. The parameters, including Von Mises stress, shear stress, pressure, and velocity, were identified and assigned to each cost function of the 12 models. Finally, the Nelder-Mead algorithm was applied to rank the twelve models based on a weighted multi-criteria score. The results demonstrate that the conducted in silico framework serves as an effective high-throughput screening tool for selecting scaffold architectures that provide a favorable biophysical microenvironment balancing mechanical resilience with perfusion-driven mechanobiological stimuli before costly in vitro experimentation. While limited to a parametric set of twelve configurations, it provides a proof-of-concept demonstration of the effectiveness of combining DOE, CFD, FEM, and Nelder-Mead ranking for selecting the best-ranked internal architecture within the investigated set; specifically the combination of body-centered struts and square cross-sectional profiles, for bone tissue engineering 3D substitutes. The macroscopic envelope geometries (cubic and rectangular prismatic) serve only as parametric spacers and are not intended to represent clinically prescriptive external shapes; anisotropy was not investigated in this proof-of-concept study and remains a subject for future work with expanded design spaces. The results demonstrate the superiority of the body-centered scaffold with square cross-sectional struts (Model M11) across nearly all mechanical and fluid dynamic criteria. While the design space in this proof-of-concept study is limited to 12 categorical configurations, the ranking framework, formally defined with a clear design vector, objective function, and constraints, identified the best-ranked architecture among the twelve candidates. This framework can be readily extended to larger design spaces with continuous variables (e.g., pore size, strut thickness, porosity) and additional performance metrics. Specifically, it outperforms the majority of models in minimizing Von Mises stress and maximizing shear rate, pressure distribution, and fluid velocity. The results could be tested further in in vitro and in vivo studies.

works.title: Plug-and-Play or Plug-and-Pray? Impact of random versus targeted integration on the linearity and orthogonality of synthetic gene circuits in CHO cells
works.abstract: Predictable and tuneable gene expression is essential for advanced mammalian cell engineering yet remains challenged by genomic position effects and copy number variability. This study systematically compares random integration (RI) and targeted integration (TI) of two synthetic lineariser gene circuits, TetR/eGFP_Lin and PhlFd/mCherry_Lin, in CHO-S cells. Both circuits exhibited strong linearity and orthogonality across integration strategies, but integration method and repressor choice produced distinct performance trade-offs. RI increased achievable dynamic range for PhlFd but increased basal leakiness for TetR, whereas TI, via a dual-landing-pad system, constrained copy number, and reduced basal expression and PhlFd expression variability. These findings highlight integration context and circuit architecture as key design parameters informing rational design of synthetic regulators for biopharmaceutical applications.

works.title: Screening a thermotolerant Komagataella phaffii strain with methanol cross-tolerance and the associated physiological and transcriptional responses
works.abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a prominent methylotrophic yeast widely used in industrial biotechnology for heterologous protein production, chemical synthesis, and C1 feedstock utilization. However, its industrial application is limited by thermal stress and methanol toxicity, while the relationship between heat adaptation and methanol tolerance remains poorly understood. Here, we obtained a thermotolerant mutant ATH through ARTP mutagenesis followed by adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) under heat stress (37 °C). ATH tolerated heat and methanol robustly under individual stress conditions, achieving 3-fold and 8-fold higher cell densities than GS115 at 37 °C or in 5% (v/v) methanol, respectively, yet failed under the combined stress of 37 °C and 5% methanol. Using three proteins (GFP, OPH, and ChiA) as reporters, we found that ATH showed higher heterologous expression than GS115 at 33 °C. Physiologically, ATH displayed enhanced cell wall/membrane integrity, reduced ROS accumulation and lower lipid peroxidation (>30% reduction in MDA), and accelerated formaldehyde clearance. Transcriptomics identified 561 shared differentially expressed genes, with coordinated upregulation of heat shock proteins (HSP70/40/90 families; Hsp104 and Hsp70-SSA2), antioxidant enzymes (catalase, peroxiredoxin), and cell wall/membrane remodeling genes, alongside downregulation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis. Whole-genome resequencing further distinguished ATH from GS115 by only 19 variants (9 SNPs and 10 InDels), highlighting a compact genetic basis for the evolved phenotype. This work provides a K. phaffii chassis with improved individual heat and methanol tolerance and elucidates the physiological, transcriptional, and genomic mechanism underlying heat–methanol cross-adaptation.

works.title: Phospholipase Fluorogenic Probes and Molecular Determinants of Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate–Adenosine Monophosphate Binding to Cyclic Oligonucleotide-Based Antiphage Signaling System CapV
works.abstract: Cyclic oligonucleotide-based antiphage signaling systems (CBASS) protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection by producing cyclic nucleotide second messengers that activate downstream effector proteins. Cyclic guanosine monophosphate-adenosine monophosphate (cGAMP)-activated phospholipase in Vibrio (CapV) is a prevalent CBASS effector whose activity is commonly monitored using the commercially available fluorogenic substrate resorufin butyrate; however, this probe is hydrolyzed by both basal and activated CapV, limiting its usefulness in CapV-related studies. Here, we report the rational design and evaluation of a series of resorufin ester probes with varying acyl chain lengths to improve the fluorogenic assay used to monitor CapV (from Acinetobacter baumannii and Vibrio cholerae) activation. While resorufin butyrate and pentanoate exhibited substantial cGAMP-independent hydrolysis, resorufin octanoate and decanoate provided an optimal balance between catalytic turnover and activation-dependent discrimination, displaying over 5-fold and approximately 10-fold increases in hydrolysis, respectively, upon 3',3'-cGAMP activation. Using resorufin octanoate as a fluorogenic reporter, we systematically investigated the effects of cyclic dinucleotide structural modifications on CapV activation. Phosphorothioate analogues with nonbridging sulfur (exo-S linkages) retained partial agonist activity, whereas the corresponding bridging 5'-phosphorothioester (endo-S) analogues was inactive, highlighting the importance of the native phosphodiester moiety in activating CapV. Replacement of the ribose 2'-hydroxyl groups with fluorine preserved CapV activation, whereas 2'-deoxy substitutions reduced activity, with modifications on the adenosine moiety having a greater detrimental effect than those on guanosine. These findings using the fluorogenic probes were validated using phospholipid hydrolysis and activity-based protein labeling assays. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the observed activity trends arise from differential disruption of key hydrogen-bonding interactions and ligand conformations required for productive CapV activation. Together, these fluorogenic probes provide a robust, high-throughput-compatible platform for studying CapV activation and defining cyclic dinucleotide structure-activity relationships.

works.title: Benzo[ c ]acridine Dimer Cyclization as a Route toward a Small Bicationic Heteroaromatic Compound with Unprecedented G-Quadruplex Stabilization Properties
works.abstract: G-quadruplex (G4) DNA structures are key regulatory elements in genome stability and gene expression, with a pronounced role in cancer biology due to their selective formation in oncogenic genomic regions and abundance in tumor cells. Their structural uniqueness makes them compelling targets for therapeutic intervention. Thus, targeting G4s with small molecule ligands offers a promising approach for modulating gene expression and inducing replication stress, particularly in DNA damage response-deficient malignancies such as ovarian and breast cancers. However, the structural diversity of G4s has hindered the development of ligands capable of broad-spectrum, topology-independent stabilization. Here, we introduce a novel dimeric N-methylbenzo[c]acridinium derivative, engineered as a visible-light-absorbing cationic G4 ligand. Compared to previously reported diazonia derivatives, this compound demonstrates red-shifted optical properties, superior luminescence quantum efficiency, and outstanding G4-stabilizing activity. It exhibits high preferential binding for G4s over dsDNA, induces conformational transitions between hybrid and antiparallel G4s, stalls DNA replication, and disrupts DNA duplex formation. Notably, its broad, topology-independent recognition enables stabilization of a range of G4 targets. Crucially, it surpasses benchmark G4 ligands, including PhenDC3 and CX-5461, in both selectivity and/or efficacy. These results support the dimeric benzo[c]acridinium scaffold as a versatile platform for the development of G4-targeted therapeutic strategies.
